# Intake Brief: Promo video scenarios (10+)

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map
**Status:** CONFIRMED — producer answered Q1 (b), Q2 (c), Q3 (a) on AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA.

## Problem statement

The game can record bot-flown gameplay clips (`npm run capture`) and compile
them into a promo, showreel and highlights (`compile-promo`), and the footage
can only show what the current run happens to contain. Today the only dev
scenarios are capture shortcuts (`boss`, `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) that jump
to an already-terminal boss fight; there is no curated set of scenes that
showcases the game's range. A promo video therefore needs dedicated,
reproducible scenarios — each pairing an interesting ship configuration with a
deliberate enemy wave — that the Watch Demo and the capture tooling can drive
on demand.

## Users

- **Producer / marketing** — wants a selection of visually distinct, reliably
  capturable moments to assemble into a promo video without hand-playing runs.
- **Player of Watch Demo** — sees varied, interesting bot-flown gameplay in the
  attract loop rather than the same default run each time.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, I want to record a boss battle, a pick-up frenzy and a dense
  enemy horde from fixed, reproducible scenarios so the promo covers each
  editorial category.
- As a player, I want the Watch Demo to fly a variety of bot/loadout and enemy
  combinations so the attract loop shows off the game's range.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (ten scenarios):** At least 10 scenarios are registered in the shared
  registry (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) and resolvable via the existing
  `scenario` URL query parameter, dev-gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV`
  exactly like today's scenarios — a production build and a normal run are
  unchanged.
- **AC2 (composition):** Every scenario starts from (i) the **single shipped
  ship config** paired with a **curated bot-tuning preset** in `src/data/
  bot-tuning.json` (optionally a starting weapon/loadout where existing
  mechanics support it) and (ii) a **hand-authored promo wave definition**
  composed from the existing spawner/movement machinery; each scenario is
  deterministic for a given seed and **bot-pilotable end to end**, sustaining
  enough watchable footage for a promo cut (target ≥45 s of action before the
  demo game-over dwell).
- **AC3 (range):** The scenario set evidences every promo editorial category
  from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` (`weapons`, `pickups`, `enemies`, `boss`) with at
  least one scenario each, and the set is ordered to open with a high
  action-intensity hook so the first captured cut has no dead air.
- **AC4 (capture integration):** `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` lists
  every scenario with its one-line effect, and `npm run capture --
  --all-scenarios` records one clean clip per scenario.
- **AC5 (tests):** Hermetic tests pin registry ↔ resolver parity, each
  scenario's bot-tuning preset and wave definition, and dev-only gating; an
  integration/demo check confirms a scenario is flown by the Watch Demo bot.
- **AC6 (docs):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, capture `--help` and
  `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.
- **AC7 (suite):** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scenarios are **dev-only**: gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV` exactly like
  today's scenarios (`src/core/devScenario.ts`); the shipped bundle stays
  inert.
- Single source of truth remains `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`; the game
  resolver and the capture CLI must not drift (registry ↔ resolver parity
  test enforced).
- Scenarios are **bot-flown** (the Watch Demo bot / competent bot), reproducible
  per seed, and must not require a human pilot to produce good footage.
- **Wave definitions are new hand-authored content**, but must be composed from
  the **existing spawner/movement machinery** (V/diver swarm, centipede, ghost,
  harvester, horde, strike, lane traffic, asteroid, boss/minion classes) — no
  new gameplay behaviour, so the gym↔game parity and duplicate-body guards in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` are not triggered.
- The shipped ship config (`ship-config.csv`) is **unchanged**; variety comes
  from bot-tuning presets and loadouts, not new ship rows.

## Existing state

- Ship configs: **one** row in `src/data/ship-config.csv` (asteroids scheme,
  thrust 300 px/s², maxSpeed 175 px/s). ShipConfig shape: `configTypes.ts:372`.
- Bot tuning: named presets via `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`, persisted in
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (currently one `Default` preset with `competent`
  + `human` layers); Watch Demo flies the current preset
  (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL).
- Waves: static `LEVELS` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), data-driven difficulty
  curves (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) sequenced by
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`; spawners per movement class in `src/waves/`.
- Power-ups/weapons: 16 power-up ids and 12 weapon drop ids
  (`src/powerups/types.ts`).
- Scenario infra: registry `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (3 entries),
  resolver `src/core/devScenario.ts`, capture CLI `--scenario /
  --list-scenarios / --all-scenarios`, page-side handle
  `window.__aiHellScenario` to release frozen runs.

## Desired change

Extend the dev-scenario registry so each entry carries the **bot-tuning preset
name** (and optional start loadout) plus its **hand-authored wave definition**
and optional seed. A new promo-wave module (`src/waves/promoScenarios.*`
naming TBD at implementation) hosts the hand-authored definitions, each built
from the existing spawner classes; the scenario resolver applies them at run
start through the existing seams (ship config loading, bot-tuning application,
wave sequencing, run seeding) rather than adding new gameplay. The result is a
catalogue of ≥10 named, documented promo scenarios driveable by
`npm run capture -- --scenario <name>` and the Watch Demo, covering all four
editorial categories and ordered to open with a high-intensity hook.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` — extend registry entries with bot-tuning
  preset + wave definition + optional loadout/seed metadata.
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts` — types for the richer entries.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — resolve and apply the preset and wave at run
  start; extend the resolved-scenario union.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` / `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — curated presets
  per scenario (Q1 answer: single ship, varied presets).
- `src/waves/` — new hand-authored promo wave definitions reusing existing
  spawner/movement classes, with tests (Q2 answer).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — scenario application seam at run start.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `--help`, README — documentation (AC6).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** scenarios are surfaced via the existing registry/URL-param
  pattern plus the capture CLI — no new menu picker unless requested (scope
  creep risk if a visible picker is added later; record as a separate item).
- **Assumption (Q1):** "interesting ship configuration" is delivered through
  bot-tuning/loadout variety on the single shipped ship — no new ShipConfig
  rows. Loadout variety limited to what existing mechanics support.
- **Assumption (Q2):** hand-authored waves live in a new dev-gated module
  composed from existing spawners — content, not new behaviour.
- **Risk:** hand-authored waves must be calibrated so the competent bot
  survives and keeps collecting — a scenario the bot dies in instantly is a
  wasted clip; the ≥45 s sustained-footage target implies some scenarios span
  several waves with the demo game-over dwell only at the end.
- **Risk:** promo footage reads as repetitive if the wave set is a flat list of
  similar archetypes — AC3's category mapping and an intense opening mitigate.
- **Scope-creep risk:** an attract-mode playlist / menu picker for these
  scenarios is out of scope for this item; create a linked follow-up if wanted.

## Related work

- AH-0MV6JGE9R005YOL1 Shared scenario registry and contract tests (completed)
- AH-0MUZM8ATZ002AKFP Batch scenario listing and multi-video capture (completed)
- AH-0MV6JGQFK007MXGX Add --all-scenarios batch capture (completed)
- AH-0MVDV4RJ300459ZF Editorial config and feature-coverage manifest (completed)
- AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18 Implement: pure edit-plan and selection logic in compile-promo (completed)
- AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4 Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips (completed)
- AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (completed)
- AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 Add 5 new levels before the boss showcasing the classic-arcade enemy roster (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Ship configurations: only one ShipConfig exists today. Where should the
  'interesting ship configuration' per scenario come from? (a) Author 2–4
  additional ShipConfig rows; (b) Keep the single ship; vary the
  bot-tuning/loadout preset instead; (c) Both." —
  **Answer (producer): (b) Keep the single ship; vary the bot-tuning/loadout
  preset instead.** Source: interactive reply on the work item, 2026-10-27.
  Research: `src/data/ship-config.csv` has one row; `botTuningStore` supports
  named presets (`bot-tuning.json`); Watch Demo already flies the current
  preset. Final ACs reflect preset/loadout variety, no new ship rows.
- Q2: "Enemy waves: where do the waves come from? (a) Reuse existing campaign
  content plus a few hand-authored waves; (b) Reuse existing content only;
  (c) Hand-author all new promo-tailored wave definitions." —
  **Answer (producer): (c) Hand-author all new promo-tailored wave
  definitions.** Source: interactive reply on the work item, 2026-10-27.
  Research: spawner/movement classes exist per archetype in `src/waves/`;
  hand-authored definitions reuse them, keeping the parity guards quiet.
- Q3: "'Wide range of experiences': how should the 10+ scenarios be defined?
  (a) Map across the promo editorial categories (weapons, pickups, enemies,
  boss), open with a high-intensity hook; (b) Showcase specific enemy
  archetypes without category mapping; (c) Simplest 10+ slots." —
  **Answer (producer): (a) Map across editorial categories; open with a high
  action-intensity hook.** Source: interactive reply on the work item,
  2026-10-27. Research: `EDITORIAL_CONFIG.categories` in
  `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`; the coverage manifest requires every category
  to be evidenced.

# Intake brief — Explosions should be explosions (image-based explosion VFX)

> **Source request (verbatim):** "The explosions right now are just multiple
> circles. They look OK but we can improve them a great deal. Make them actual
> explosion images that change shape as they shrink. Each should be a subtle
> variation on the red/orange explosion colour."

## Problem statement

Every destruction burst is still rendered as a cloud of small filled circles,
so explosions read as "a lot of dots" rather than as an explosion. Replace the
circle particles with image-based explosion shapes whose silhouette changes as
they shrink and fade, keep each entity's hue on the outer lobes/embers, and give
every burst a red/orange fire core with subtle per-particle variation
(producer decision Q2 = b).

## Users

- **Player** — the primary user; perceives destruction feedback.
  - *As a player, when I destroy an enemy or lose my ship, I see a recognisable
    explosion (a hot core, ragged flame lobes, sparks) rather than a spray of
    dots, so combat impact feels real and satisfying.*
- **Developer / designer** — tunes the look without touching gameplay code.
  - *As a developer, I can adjust the fire palette, frame count, morph timing
    and particle counts through named exported constants in one shared module
    and verify the behaviour deterministically in unit tests.*
- **Agent / maintainer** — must be able to change the look once.
  - *As a maintainer, I know the game and every gym consume the same VFX code,
    so a look change cannot drift between the game and the gym scenes.*

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-11-03)

The three questions that materially change the implementation were answered by
the producer on 2026-11-03; AC1–AC3 below are revised to match, and the answers
are recorded in the Appendix.

1. **Art source — (a) procedural runtime-generated textures.** Explosion frames
   are generated in code into cached Phaser textures. No binary art is
   committed and no asset/attribution pipeline is introduced.
2. **Colour policy — (b) keep the per-entity base hue, add a red/orange hot
   core.** Outer lobes and embers keep the exploding entity's palette colour
   with the existing seeded HSL jitter, so per-entity identity is preserved
   (AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034 stays in force); a distinct hot core layer is coloured
   from the exported warm red/orange → white-hot palette. Explosions therefore
   read as a fiery blast without discarding "that ship" identity.
3. **Coverage — (a) all `spawnExplosionParticles` call sites** (enemy, boss,
   mini-boss and drone deaths, player death, victory fireworks, wave-timeout
   penalty, and every gym), because a single shared module keeps gym↔game
   parity.

## Existing state

- All destruction VFX route through one shared module,
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` (`spawnExplosionParticles()`). The eight
  production call sites are `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`,
  `src/entities/Boss.ts`, `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (`_spawnPlayerExplosion`),
  `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts`, `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` and
  `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` (victory fireworks/defeat; imported by the gyms via
  the shared combat core), so game↔gym parity already holds.
- A burst is a **single Phaser `Graphics`** animated by one tween; each frame
  redraws every live particle as `fillCircle(p.x, p.y, p.radius)` with a
  colour from `jitterColor(baseColor)` (HSL jitter ±`EXPLOSION_HUE_JITTER_DEG`
  = 20° around the exploding entity's palette colour). Particles fade
  (`1 - fadeStep·elapsed`) and shrink over `EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS` (400 ms).
- Three patterns exist (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`) mapped per entity in
  `EXPLOSION_PATTERNS_BY_TYPE`; counts scale with entity size (clamped 8–80).
- Determinism: all jitter is drawn from a seeded PRNG (`createRng(seed)`), and
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` pins geometry, colour bands, counts,
  jitter and the Phaser integration through a structural scene double.
- Live per-kind counts are exposed by `getExplosionVfxCounts()` /
  `resetExplosionVfxCounts()` and consumed by the action-intensity metric.
- The repo ships **no sprite/atlas image assets** today: `public/` contains
  baked audio (`public/audio/sfx/*.wav`) and photo backgrounds
  (`public/assets/backgrounds/*.jpg`, NASA public domain, licence in
  `public/assets/backgrounds/ATTRIBUTION.md`); every *vector* visual is drawn
  procedurally (Graphics / shapes) and no explosion imagery exists anywhere.
  Audio is baked from ToneForge recipes by `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
  (Corrected during planning: the intake brief overstated this as audio-only.)
- Documentation of the current circle rendering lives in
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.1–§7.2 (particle-effects and
  explosion-patterns bullets) and `README.md` ("Explosion VFX (particle
  bursts)").

## Desired change

1. Replace circle particles with **explosion imagery**: a small set of
   explosion shapes (e.g. 4–6 frames per burst family) whose silhouette changes
   over the burst's life as the particle shrinks and fades, so the explosion
   visibly *evolves* (hot dense core → ragged flame lobes → thin embers)
   instead of uniformly shrinking dots.
2. Add a **red/orange fire core** to every burst: the inner/core particles use
   a warm palette (deep red → orange → white-hot, with subtle per-particle
   hue/lightness variation inside the documented warm band), while the outer
   lobes and embers keep the exploding entity's palette hue with the existing
   seeded HSL jitter (`EXPLOSION_HUE_JITTER_DEG` ±20°). Producer decision
   Q2 = (b).
3. Keep the existing pattern system (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`), counts,
   lifespan, seeded determinism, teardown/registry contract and per-kind
   counters intact — this is a rendering/feel change, not a gameplay change.
4. Apply the change through the single shared module so the game and every gym
   get it automatically (no divergent copies).

## Acceptance Criteria

> AC1–AC3 reflect the producer's 2026-11-03 decisions: (Q1 = a) procedural
> runtime textures, (Q2 = b) entity hue retained with a red/orange hot core,
> (Q3 = a) every call site.

- [ ] **AC1 — Explosion imagery replaces circles.** `spawnExplosionParticles()`
  renders each particle as an explosion shape from cached, shared textures/frames
  **generated procedurally at runtime** by the new texture helper (no committed
  image files, no per-frame `fillCircle` particle rendering); a burst visibly
  reads as a blast (core + lobes/embers), not as a cloud of circles.
- [ ] **AC2 — Shape changes as the particle shrinks.** Each particle's shape
  frame is a deterministic function of its normalised age only (frame index and
  any seeded frame offset reproducible from the same `opts.seed`), so the
  silhouette morphs through at least 3 distinct frames from spawn to expiry while
  the particle also scales/shrinks; the final state is a thin ember, not a dot.
- [ ] **AC3 — Entity hue retained, red/orange hot core added.** Every burst has
  two colour zones: (i) **core** particles coloured from exported warm-palette
  constants — 100 % inside the documented red/orange hue band with bounded
  saturation/lightness variance and a brighter white-hot centre; and (ii)
  **lobe/ember** particles whose colours stay within `EXPLOSION_HUE_JITTER_DEG`
  of the exploding entity's base colour with the existing
  `EXPLOSION_SAT_VARIANCE` / `EXPLOSION_LIGHT_VARIANCE` bounds. Tests assert both
  band invariants over every colour the module emits, for death bursts *and*
  victory fireworks.
- [ ] **AC4 — Behaviour preserved.** Pattern assignment, size-scaled counts
  (8–80), `EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS`, seeded reproducibility (same seed ⇒ identical
  frames/colours/positions), the `opts.registry` teardown contract, the
  `getExplosionVfxCounts()` increments/decrements, the `delay`/`depth`/`scale`
  options and the null-scene guard all behave exactly as before.
- [ ] **AC5 — Single shared implementation / parity.** The change lives only in
  the shared VFX module (+ its texture helper); the game and every gym use it
  with no duplicated rendering code, and the repo-wide duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and gym-parity docs
  assertions still pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Deterministic, headless-testable tests.** Unit tests cover frame
  selection/morph progression, colour-band invariants, determinism, teardown and
  counters without a real WebGL canvas (texture provider is injectable/stubbable
  and preserves the existing structural scene double), and an in-game/gym visual
  verification is documented (GymFodderEnemies death bursts, player death,
  victory fireworks).
- [ ] **AC7 — Performance budget.** Concurrency stays bounded: no per-particle
  texture generation, frame textures are generated once and reused, and no
  regression in particle counts or teardown (no leaked display objects after
  scene SHUTDOWN/restart).
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation updated.** GDD §7.1–§7.2 (particle effects,
  explosion-patterns/colour table), the README "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)"
  section and the module header/comments describe the image-based look, the
  frame/morph constants and the two-zone colour model (warm red/orange core +
  entity-hue lobes), replacing the "small filled circles" and flat per-entity
  colour statements while keeping the "hues stay recognisably 'that ship'"
  statement scoped to lobes/embers.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No new runtime dependency**; stay on Phaser primitives.
- **Zero-binary-asset convention** (producer decision Q1 = a): generate the
  explosion frame textures at runtime from code, cached by key; do not commit
  binary art or add an asset pipeline.
- **GDD §7.1 style rule**: "Geometric, angular shapes … No organic forms".
  Literal photographic/smoke-puff explosion images would conflict; the
  procedural frames therefore use a stylised neon blast (angular/ragged polygon
  lobes) to stay within the established art language.
- **Gym↔game parity** (repo convention / AGENTS.md): one shared code path.
- **Determinism**: seeded PRNG only; no `Math.random()` in VFX.
- **Performance**: bursts can be dense (Boss layers 3 patterns, victory
  fireworks up to 30 staggered bursts); textured particles must not multiply
  draw calls per particle in a way that breaks the current action-intensity
  budget. Use shared textures + batched images, and keep the existing count
  clamps.
- **Scope discipline**: gameplay numbers (damage, counts, timing, SFX) are out
  of scope; extra ideas are recorded as linked work items, not folded in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — replace the Graphics circle renderer with a
  pre-generated/cached explosion frame texture provider and per-particle
  image/quad rendering whose frame is a function of normalised age; add the
  warm-palette constants + colour resolution; keep the pure geometry/PRNG,
  pattern, lifecycle, registry and counter contracts.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` — extend/extend-and-rename the pure-state
  and Phaser-double tests for frames, morph progression, colour band,
  determinism, teardown and counters.
- `src/vfx/explosionTextures.ts` (new, predicted) — procedural frame generation
  (deterministic polygon/blob silhouettes per frame) plus the texture cache/
  keyed registry and a headless-safe seam.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — the warm fire palette constants (or keep them in the
  VFX module, following the module's existing constant-export convention).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.1–§7.2 particle-effects and explosion
  pattern/colour text.
- `README.md` — "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)" section.
- Call sites that need no code change but must be visually verified:
  `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`,
  `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` (victory fireworks).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ambiguity risk — resolved 2026-11-03.** The producer chose Q2 = (b): keep
  the per-entity hue (Scout green, Diver yellow, Phaser magenta, player cyan,
  Boss red …) for lobes/embers and add a red/orange hot core. Per-entity identity
  is therefore retained, AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034 stays in force, and the GDD colour
  table gains a core band rather than being rewritten.
- **GDD style conflict risk** — "no organic forms" vs. explosion images; the
  recommended stylised-neon-blast silhouette keeps the language, but a producer
  preference for realistic puffs would require an art pipeline.
- **Performance risk** — replacing one Graphics with N images per burst could
  regress frame time in dense scenes (Boss + fireworks). Mitigation: shared
  cached textures, a bounded texture count, batched rendering, and a check of
  the action-intensity/perf capture before review.
- **Test harness risk** — texture generation needs a canvas; the procedural
  option must expose an injectable provider so headless Vitest runs stay
  deterministic and do not need WebGL.
- **Scope-creep risk** — tempting extras (screen-shake per particle, heat
  distortion, sound layering, per-entity explosion image families) are recorded
  as linked follow-up items, not added here.
- **Assumption** — the operator's "each should be a subtle variation on the
  red/orange explosion colour" refers to per-particle colour variation inside a
  warm palette, not a single flat orange.

## Related work

- **Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths**
  (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V) — the parent feature that introduced the circle-based
  particle bursts this item replaces visually.
- **Explosion pattern emitters and combinator** (AH-0MTVID632005ACBF) —
  `radial`/`ring`/`implosion` geometry that must be preserved.
- **Explosion particle test suite** (AH-0MTVH6DQO0016CGJ) — the test-first
  contract this change must extend rather than break.
- **Entity-centred explosion colour jitter** (AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034) — the
  per-entity hue jitter, which the producer decisions keep in force for
  lobes/embers; only the new core layer is warm-palette rather than entity-hued.
- **Add randomness to explosion** (AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH) — seeded size/position
  jitter that must remain deterministic.
- **Parity: gym↔game verification + explosion registry** (AH-0MUZQGRQR0086NP6)
  — the per-kind counter and parity guards that this change must keep green.
- **Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory** (AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44) and
  **Explosions timed with the beat** (AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3) — other consumers of
  `spawnExplosionParticles` whose look/behaviour must stay coherent.
- Related docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.1–§7.2, `README.md`
  (Explosion VFX), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§8.5 gym surface),
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` (VFX counters).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V** – Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths (completed)
- **AH-0MTVID632005ACBF** – Explosion pattern emitters and combinator (completed)
- **AH-0MTVH6DQO0016CGJ** – Explosion particle test suite (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.1–§7.2 explosion VFX/particle docs
- `README.md` — "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)" section
- `CHANGELOG.md` — release history

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Q1–Q3 were answered by the producer on 2026-11-03 (interactive reply, this plan
session); Q4–Q5 were answered by agent research during intake. No OPEN QUESTIONs
remain.

- **Q1 (art source).** How should the explosion imagery be produced?
  (a) Procedurally generated at runtime into cached Phaser textures — keeps the
  repo's zero-asset convention and determinism; (b) committed raster sprite
  sheets/atlases under `public/` — needs an art source and an asset pipeline;
  (c) Graphics-only morphing polygons — lightest, but not really "images".
  **Recommended:** (a) — the repo ships no *sprite* image assets, all VFX are
  code-drawn, and this keeps the seeded/deterministic test contract and
  gym↔game parity intact.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-11-03, interactive reply): **(a) procedural
  runtime-generated textures**. Final: (a).
- **Q2 (colour policy).** Should explosions drop the per-entity hue (Scout green,
  Diver yellow, Tank orange, Phaser magenta, Swarm blue, Boss red, player cyan)
  in favour of a red/orange fire palette with subtle per-particle variation?
  (a) Yes, every explosion becomes red/orange variants; (b) keep the entity hue
  as the base but add a red/orange hot core; (c) red/orange for enemy-death
  bursts only, keep player cyan and multi-colour victory fireworks.
  **Recommended:** (a) — matches the operator's wording ("subtle variation on
  the red/orange explosion colour") and the "explosions should look like
  explosions" intent; note (a) would intentionally supersede

# Intake brief — Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)

## Headline

Replace the mini-boss reward choice with a **spin-the-wheel** that always
delivers a guaranteed permanent upgrade: one bonus slot upgrades everything,
5 slots upgrade 3 picks, 10 upgrade 2, and the remaining 84 upgrade 1 — so a
mini-boss victory always makes the build meaningfully stronger.

## Problem statement

Mini-boss rewards currently offer a flat menu (upgrade any one owned item, or
unlock one locked weapon) which reads as a low-value chore rather than a
reward. The player wants a moment of anticipation that *always* pays out in
power, presented as a wheel of fortune spin over the power-ups the player has
invested in permanent slots.

## Users

- **Player (core loop):** after defeating a mini-boss, expects a celebration
  and a guaranteed, tangible power gain.
- **Demo/attract bot:** must not stall on the wheel; auto-spins after the same
  human-like delay as the hold-full choice (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F contract).

### Example user story

> As a player, when I defeat a mini-boss, I want to click a button to spin a
> wheel showing the power-ups in my permanent slots, watch it slow to a stop,
> and receive the landed upgrade(s) — so the reward feels like a gamble that
> always pays out, not a to-do list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Defeating a mini-boss opens a **wheel overlay** (the multi-option upgrade-or-unlock choice is gone): one wedge per **owned permanent kind** across the shared six-slot pool — power-up kinds **and** weapon drops — plus a single **bonus** wedge; play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice.
- Spinning is player-initiated (click/keyboard), the wheel animation starts fast and eases out (building tension; the outcome must not be predictable until it stops), and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly once.
- The spin outcome follows the **100-slot distribution**: 1 slot = bonus (every owned permanent kind +1 level), 5 slots = 3 upgrades, 10 slots = 2 upgrades, 84 slots = 1 upgrade. Multi-upgrade slots pick **distinct** owned kinds where possible and repeat a kind only when there are fewer owned kinds than the slot's count (a player with one owned power-up landing a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
- **Empty-owned fallback:** when the player owns no permanent kinds at a mini-boss defeat, the wheel is not shown and the existing hold-full-style three-option choice is offered instead, so a mini-boss always pays out.
- The run-scoped weapon-unlock feature and its reward options are **removed** from mini-boss rewards (locked-pool option builders, `getUnlockedWeapons` and the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field; `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bumped so stale checkpoints are rejected cleanly).
- Outcomes are drawn from the **run-seeded RNG** (no `Math.random()`), the distribution/resolver and the reward application live in shared modules the game and gyms both consume, and demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md`, checkpoint notes), including code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, including unit tests for the slot distribution/outcome resolver and PlayScene wheel-flow tests replacing the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): slot distribution and reward
  application must live once in shared modules consumed by `PlayScene` and any
  gym surface; no scene-private divergence.
- **Code-first visuals:** icons come from the existing code-drawn
  `src/powerups/icons.ts` (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets (GDD §7.2).
- **Seed reproducibility:** run-seeded RNG only; deterministic tests.
- **Launcher-agnostic overlay:** a single optional selection/result callback
  (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s `onSelect`), so any launcher can drive it.
- No ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation (test-slot policy); changed
  scope is run via the test skill.

## Existing state

- Defeating a mini-boss fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` → `openMiniBossReward`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`), which offers **one** upgrade-or-unlock choice:
  every owned permanent weapon/power-up level-up offer (built by
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`) plus every still-locked weapon from
  `MINI_BOSS_LOCKED_WEAPONS` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`). The overlay is the
  shared `MineralChoiceScene`; selection applies `applyMineralChoiceReward`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`, re-exported by
  `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`). Rewards are applied exactly once
  (`selectMiniBossReward` resets the open flag). See GDD §4.4.4
  (AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH).
- **Note (stale description):** the description's "choice of 5 random power
  ups" does not match current behaviour — the live reward is the
  upgrade-or-unlock menu described above; the wheel replaces *that*.
- Each wheel-relevant decision is a permanent kind in a **shared 6-slot pool**
  (`src/powerups/slots.ts`) covering both power-up kinds and weapon drops;
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) tracks permanent vs
  temporary levels and per-kind caps; the checkpoint
  (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) persists weapon/power-up levels and
  `unlockedWeapons` (the latter is removed by AC5).
- Demo mode already auto-selects the reward via `_randomDemoRewardIndex()`
  after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) — reuse this
  seam for auto-spin.

## Desired change

- New pure module (e.g. `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`): the 100-slot
  distribution (1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single), a weighted
  outcome resolver over owned permanent kinds, distinct-kind multi-upgrade
  selection (repeats only when fewer kinds than picks), cap-aware handling,
  injectable RNG.
- New launcher-agnostic overlay (e.g. `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`): one
  wedge per owned icon plus the bonus wedge, pointer, fast-starting/eased-out
  spin, landed-wedge highlight, click/keyboard to spin, result callback.
  Register in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward`: launch the
  wheel with the owned permanent kinds (from `resolveSlotState`/
  `getWeaponLevels`/`getPowerUpLevels`), apply the resolved outcome once
  through the shared reward machinery, fall back to the three-option choice
  when nothing is owned, and keep demo auto-spin.
- Remove the unlock feature (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts` locked-pool state and
  option builders, `PlayScene.getUnlockedWeapons`, the checkpoint
  `unlockedWeapons` field) and bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- Update GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` and checkpoint docs.
- Replace the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests in
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`; add deterministic unit tests for the
  distribution and outcome resolver.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — rework `openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward` to the wheel flow; fallback; demo auto-spin; drop unlock state.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (new) — pure 100-slot distribution + weighted outcome resolver, distinct-kind picks, caps.
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new) — launcher-agnostic wheel overlay: wedges, spin + ease-out animation, pointer, result callback.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — reuse `drawPowerUpIcon`/`drawWeaponIcon` for wheel wedges.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — owned permanent kinds feeding the wheel population.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — unlock machinery to be removed (AC5).
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` / `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — shared reward application for spin outcomes.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register the wheel scene.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — remove `unlockedWeapons`; bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — exercise the shared wheel/reward path (parity).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` (new) — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool (current behaviour being replaced).
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — AI bot reward-screen selection (demo auto-select contract to preserve).
- AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF — six-slot permanent loadout accounting (slot pool the wheel reads).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — power-up level store (permanent levels/caps applied by the wheel).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (shared modules requirement).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice overlay (pattern the wheel scene mirrors).

- AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD — Mini-boss/boss strength scales with player firepower (completed; adjacent balance context for reward power).
- AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y — Show current upgrades on the hull-full screen (open; same "player must see what they own" UI concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk:** celebration VFX/audio for the spin and rebalancing the
  1/5/10/84 split are follow-ups — record as separate work items, not scope.
- **Assumption (cap-aware draws):** when a drawn kind has hit its level cap,
  re-draw a non-capped owned kind; if every owned kind is capped the spin
  grants a fallback (minerals). Confirm during planning.
- **Assumption (mandatory spin):** the wheel always grants something and has
  no skip/decline path (a refusable "reward" recreates the perceived-nothing
  outcome).
- **Risk (unlock removal):** deleting the unlock feature removes a shipped
  progression mechanic; GDD §4.4.4 and the locked-pool docs must be rewritten
  in the same change so no doc promises unlocks. `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bump
  invalidates existing checkpoints (accepted: pre-release).
- **Risk (resolver/UI drift):** the wedge list and the weighted outcome must
  be derived from the same owned-kind snapshot; the scene must never compute
  probabilities itself.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of unlock rewards.** "The wheel shows icons of power-ups the
  player has; should it fully replace the current upgrade-or-unlock choice
  (removing the run-scoped weapon-unlock feature, its locked-pool options and
  the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field)?" — **Answer (producer, interactive
  reply): Option A — fully replace.** The mini-boss reward becomes purely the
  upgrade wheel; unlock machinery is removed and `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` is
  bumped. Supersedes the options B (locked weapons as wheel outcomes) and C
  (separate secondary unlock offer). Source: producer answer, this intake
  session; recorded as AC5.
- **Q2 — Wheel population and empty-owned fallback.** "Should the wheel show
  **all** owned permanent kinds across the shared 6-slot pool (power-up kinds
  **and** weapon drops), and what happens at a mini-boss defeat when the
  player owns nothing permanent (possible at the level-1 mini-boss)?" —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): Option A** — all owned permanent
  kinds; when none are owned, fall back to the existing three-option
  hold-full-style choice so a mini-boss always pays. Options B (power-ups
  only) and C (seed the wheel with base entries) rejected. Source: producer
  answer, this intake session; recorded as AC1 + AC4.
- **Q3 — Wheel visual and weights.** "Should the wheel be 100 literal wedges,
  or a compact wheel (one wedge per owned icon + bonus wedge) whose spin
  outcome is weighted by the 100-slot distribution (1/5/10/84)?" —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): Option A** — compact wheel plus
  weighted outcome: legible UI, exact distribution preserved, multi-upgrades
  pick distinct kinds where possible. Options B (literal 100-wedge wheel) and
  C (proportional fixed wheel, accepting granularity loss) rejected. Source:
  producer answer, this intake session; recorded as AC1/AC3.

## Related-work check (duplicate detection)

Duplicate check performed (`wl search "mini-boss reward"`, `wl search
"wheel"`): no overlapping open item found — the closest items
(AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH, AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F, AH-0MVNT2Z89005OPKJ,
AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF) are completed/in-progress parents whose scope this item
extends or replaces; no duplicate.

## Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD** – Strength of mini-boss and boss should raise with the fire power of the player (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0mvj8u79v0056i2f, accept, acceptance, accounting (+351 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, accept, accounting, add, agnostic (+298 more)

## Plan (plan skill — 2026-10-28)

### Feature breakdown (test-first, dependency order)

| # | Child work item | Type | Depends on |
|---|-----------------|------|------------|
| 1 | Test the wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver (AH-0MVSF5WXQ0035NW0) | task | — |

  and hands the wheel scene the wedge list plus the resolved outcome. The
  overlay never computes probabilities, so the wedge list and the weighted
  outcome can never drift (AC1/AC3/AC6; mirrors how the choice pool is a
  single catalogue-derived source).

  choice).** `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) offers

  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`). A spin

# Intake brief — Compiled videos cannot be fast forwarded (AH-0MVMIK8EM001JAYR)

## Headline

Videos produced by `npm run capture` (MediaRecorder WebM/VP9+Opus) are
written **without a Duration element, SeekHead or Cues (seek index)**, so VLC
cannot fast-forward, seek, or even display a usable timeline for them. The fix
is a packet-preserving (`-c copy`) seek-index remux of every successful
capture output before it is delivered.

## Problem statement

Chromium's `MediaRecorder` writes a WebM stream whose Segment Info omits
Duration and whose clusters carry no external Cues/SeekHead index. Most
players tolerate this, but VLC does not: fast-forward/seeking fails,
`ffprobe` reports `duration=N/A`, and the timeline is unusable. Verified on
real capture outputs under `capture-output/` — e.g.
`capture-output/gameplay-2026-10-09T21-32-12-740Z-1.webm` has zero Cues and
zero SeekHead elements (`duration=N/A`), while the ffmpeg-compiled promos
(`capture-output/promo.webm`, `highlight-01.webm`) carry all three and are
seekable (`duration=57.896` etc.).

## Users

- The developer/producer reviewing captured gameplay footage (full runs,
  batch iterations, scenario clips, multi-scene stitched WebMs) in VLC or
  other external players.
- Any consumer of the shipped/archived WebMs who needs to scrub or fast-forward
  them without re-encoding.

User story: *As a developer reviewing captured gameplay, I want to fast-forward
and scrub through the WebM in VLC, so I can jump straight to the segments I
need instead of watching the whole clip.*

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Seekable output**: A WebM produced by `npm run capture` (with an ffmpeg
   available on the host) reports a finite non-zero total duration via
   `ffprobe -show_entries format=duration` (`format.duration`), and its EBML
   structure contains a Cues seek index plus SeekHead referencing Info,
   Tracks and Cues — verified per clip by the capture tool's existing probe.
2. **No quality/content change**: The remux is packet-preserving
   (`-c copy` — no re-encode of VP9 or Opus); codecs, stream layout, and
   decoded frame/timeline content are unchanged (verify codec + duration
   equivalence against a pre-fix capture).
3. **All capture paths benefit**: single clip, `--count` batch iterations,
   `--all-scenarios` scenario clips and the `capture:scenes` multi-scene
   stitched WebM all go through the same sink-finalise seam and are all
   seekable (they share `recording.finalise({ success: true })`).
4. **Graceful degradation**: When no ffmpeg binary can be resolved (this is
   the documented zero-ffmpeg capture environment), the capture still
   succeeds and writes the current unseekable WebM, with a clear warning
   naming the fix and how to enable it — never a hard failure that breaks
   the no-ffmpeg story.
5. **Tests + docs**: Hermetic unit tests for any new pure logic (remux
   invocation argc/verification without real footage), plus an
   integration/e2e verification on a small real clip asserting duration +
   Cues + SeekHead presence; `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (known-limits and
   output sections) and code comments updated; full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Existing documented design decision (docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md
  "No MP4 output (ffmpeg)" and `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` header): "the
  capture path never invokes a system ffmpeg". The recommended approach (a)
  keeps that constraint intact by using only the Playwright-bundled binary;
  Open Question 1 records the producer decision.
- Playwright (an existing devDependency, installed by the documented
  `npm run capture:install`) ships a **bundled ffmpeg binary** that performs
  the `-c copy` seek-index remux correctly (verified: the bundled
  `ffmpeg-linux` from the ms-playwright cache produced Duration + Cues +
  SeekHead and `duration=1.895` on a real capture). This is the recommended
  remux tool — no system install needed.
- Long-run clips can be ~1.8 GB; the sink architecture was built to keep node
  memory O(one chunk). A remux pass must stream through ffmpeg (or equivalent)
  and must not buffer the whole clip in node memory.
- Salvaged `.partial.webm` outputs are documented failure paths, not
  deliverables — out of scope.
- UK English in all written output.
- Backfill of already-captured WebMs is out of scope unless the producer
  requests it (recorded as a separate linked item if wanted).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep**: a pure-JS EBML rewriter or a backfill/`--seekable` CLI is
  larger than the reported bug. Keep the fix to the minimal remux at the
  finalise seam; record extras as linked work items, not scope.
- **Remux failure on huge clips**: a failed remux must not destroy the raw
  capture — write the remuxed file to a temp path and only swap it in on
  success (mirroring the existing `.partial.webm` rename discipline).
- **ffmpeg resolution portability**: resolution order (env → PATH → bundled
  Playwright ffmpeg) must be deterministic and documented; the bundled
  binary path depends on Playwright's install revision, so resolve it
  through the Playwright API rather than hard-coded paths.
- **Validation parity**: structural checks (duration + Cues + SeekHead) are
  automated via ffprobe; a manual VLC fast-forward check on the operator's
  machine is the final behavioural confirmation.
- **Assumption**: the reported VLC behaviour is caused by the missing
  Duration/Cues/SeekHead (confirmed structurally; see Problem statement).
  Compiled promo outputs are unaffected as they are already ffmpeg-produced.

## Existing state

`npm run capture` drives a headless Chromium page: `canvas.captureStream(60)`
→ `MediaRecorder` (VP9/Opus, 8 Mbps), chunks streamed via a bounded sink
(`scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs`) to `<stem>.partial.webm`, renamed into
place by `finalise({ success: true })`. Chromium writes no Duration/Cues.
The promo compiler (`compile-promo.mjs --compile`) already re-encodes/remuxes
its deliverables through a full ffmpeg, so promo/highlight/showreel outputs
are already seekable — only raw capture outputs are affected.

## Desired change

Attach a seek-index remux step at the sink-finalise seam so every successful
capture WebM is made seekable before it is delivered. **Decided approach (a):**
resolve the **Playwright-bundled** ffmpeg first (it is installed by the
documented `npm run capture:install` and is verified to perform this remux),
falling back to `FFMPEG_BIN`/`FFPROBE_BIN` env overrides and then PATH
(mirroring `compile-promo`'s `resolveTools()`), run
`ffmpeg -i <in>.webm -c copy <out>.webm`, swap the result in only on success,
and warn (without failing the capture) when no ffmpeg can be resolved. This
keeps the documented "never invokes a **system** ffmpeg" constraint intact.
Verification reuses the existing probe seam (`capture-probe.mjs`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` — `finalise()` seam where a seek-index
  remux would attach (or a sibling module invoked from it)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — the two sink finalise call sites
  (single-clip ~L1991 and multi-scene ~L2554); recorder setup ~L2753
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — `resolveTools()` ffmpeg-location pattern and
  the `-c copy`-style argv precedent to reuse
- `scripts/capture-probe.mjs` — existing probe seam to extend for
  duration/Cues verification
- `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.test.ts` (+ new tests) — hermetic coverage
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — update known-limits/output sections

## Related work

- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Spike: automated gameplay video capture
  (headless browser + scripted bot); established the capture pipeline.
- **AH-0MUZQG13S006KL8K** — Capture: video join + highlight selection;
  established output artefacts and the raw-WebM format.
- **AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18** — Pure edit-plan/selection logic in compile-promo;
  supplies the ffmpeg-driving pattern (incl. `resolveTools`).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documents the "no system ffmpeg in the
  capture path" constraint and the output/probe contract.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (ANSWERED — producer decision): **How should the seek-index remux relate
  to the documented "the capture path never invokes a system ffmpeg"
  constraint?** Options:
  - (a) Remux by default using the Playwright-bundled ffmpeg. The bundled
    binary (installed by the documented `npm run capture:install`) already
    performs the `-c copy` seek-index remux correctly (verified on a real
    capture: Duration + Cues + SeekHead, `duration=1.895`), so no *system*
    ffmpeg is required and the documented constraint stands literally.
    Degrade gracefully when it cannot be resolved.
  - (b) Remux by default, requiring a full system ffmpeg (compile-promo's
    `resolveTools()` path) and hard-failing the delivery when absent.
  - (c) Pure-JS EBML rewrite (patch Info/Duration, prepend SeekHead,
    append Cues) with no binary dependency at all.

  **Recommended: (a)** — smallest change, verified working, packet-preserving,
  no new dependency, and it preserves the documented constraint. `(b)` breaks
  the zero-ffmpeg capture story; `(c)` is a materially larger new
  WebM-rewriting surface (with 1.8 GB streaming-copy risk) for no benefit the
  bundled binary does not already give.

  **Answer (producer): (a)** — remux by default using the Playwright-bundled
  ffmpeg with graceful degradation. Source: interactive reply to the question
  comment (`intake - question ...` on AH-0MVMIK8EM001JAYR). The brief,
  ACs and Key Files stand as written; no further changes needed.

- Resolved without asking (answerable from repo convention — recorded as
  intake decisions, not open questions):
  - **Default vs opt-in**: the remux runs by default on every successful
    capture, because the report is about the default `npm run capture`
    output. No `--seekable` flag and no backfill command in scope.
  - **Tool resolution**: env override → bundled Playwright ffmpeg → PATH,
    following compile-promo's existing `resolveTools()` pattern
    (`FFMPEG_BIN` / `FFPROBE_BIN` first).
  - **Out of scope**: salvaged `.partial.webm` failure artefacts; backfilling
    already-captured files.

Pending the producer's answer to Q1 the brief stands as written (all
acceptance criteria are behavioural and hold under any of the three
options); the item is flagged for producer review.

**Q1 answered: (a)** — Playwright-bundled ffmpeg remux by default with
graceful degradation. The brief, ACs and Key Files are final and stand as
written.

# Bot should be aware of screen wrap around (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG)

## Problem statement

The game's playfield is a wrap-around (torus) arena — the player ship, asteroids,
bullets and raider patrol all cross a screen edge and reappear on the opposite
side — but the AI bot's decision layer (`src/ai/`) is wrap-blind: it treats the
four bounding edges as solid walls it must not approach, never crosses a seam on
purpose, and measures every distance, bearing, aim solution, threat prediction
and nearest-selection along the raw (unwrapped) straight line. A human player
routinely uses the seam to chase, flee and angle shots; the bot cannot, so demo
play looks unhuman, the bot camps near the walls it wrongly fears, and it
systematically misjudges everything on the far side of an edge.

## Users

- **Players / viewers of the attract demo** — the demo bot is deliberately
  human-like (human reaction cadence, W/A/D controls, thrust feel); humans use
  the wrap, so a bot that refuses to is conspicuous.
- **Developers** — one coherent torus model in the decision layer, so future
  features (seam-aware enemy fire, new archetypes, tuning) share a single
  implementation instead of adding seam hacks.

### Example user stories

- As a **player watching the demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge to
  reach a target that is closer the other way, so its movement looks like a
  human's.
- As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
  shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite
  edge — so engagements play out in the whole wrap-around arena.
- As a **player**, I want the bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
  across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming.
- As a **developer**, I want one wrap-aware geometry implementation used by
  steering, aim, prediction and distance, so the model is consistent and
  testable, and the headless eval measures the same physics the bot faces in
  the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wrap-aware steering (movement)** — The four arena edges stop being walls in
   the steering safety/clearance test: both the legacy `evaluateVector`
   (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) and the competent `evaluateDirection`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) no longer reject a direction
   solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`, and steering toward an
   objective uses the **shortest wrapped path** (the closer of the raw bearing
   and the seam-crossing bearing to the objective's opposite-edge duplicate) so
   the bot crosses an edge to get to the other side — used deliberately when
   net-positive (Q2), never as a scripted trick. Unit tests cover each of the
   four edges: the wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter; an
   edge-crossing direction is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.

2. **Seam-aware aim & targeting** — Aim and target selection run on the torus:
   `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the
   shortest wrapped path, and `nearestTarget` / `nearestEnemyDistance` choose
   nearest by wrapped distance. When the wrapped route to an enemy, boss or
   mineral is shorter than the raw line, the bot points at the seam duplicate —
   firing off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge. Tests assert the aim
   angle equals the wrapped-path angle when that route is shorter, and that
   behaviour is unchanged when the raw line is already shortest.

3. **Seam-aware threat & hazard prediction** — `predictIncomingFire`
   (`worldModel.ts`), the competent `closestApproach` solves and the legacy
   path-crossing checks operate on the wrapped torus, so shots and moving
   hazards whose closest approach to the player crosses a seam are predicted and
   dodged. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's existing wrap-jump clamp is
   re-verified so it does not double-compensate once positions are modelled on
   the torus. Tests: a seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening (a
   raw-line-only view would miss it).

4. **`wallMargin` retired cleanly** — The now-meaningless wall-margin tunable is
   retired (or demonstrably re-purposed) across `botDecision.ts`,
   `competent/tunables.ts`, `style/fitting.ts` and `tuningFields.ts`; saved
   bot-tuning configs (`src/data/bot-tuning.json` and any gym-saved tunings)
   still load with the field gone (unknown-field tolerance), and the style-fit
   mapping is updated per the retirement. Documented in the tuning UI/docs.

5. **Eval parity** — The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is brought
   to wrap-parity with the game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of
   being culled off-field, and hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped
   path (matching the seam-aware aim the enemy wrap epic ships), so eval scores
   measure wrap-aware play. `arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet and
   seam-aim cases.

6. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit/integration tests cover wrapped steering
   (all four edges, raw vs. wrapped), seam aim, seam threat prediction, wrapped
   nearest-selection when raw and wrapped ordering differ, wall-margin
   retirement and eval parity. The human-like governor's reaction cadence,
   controls and thrust feel are unchanged (existing steering/bot integration
   tests stay green, plus new wrap scenarios). `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` are updated to describe the wrap-aware model. The full
   project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- One shared implementation in the bot decision layer — no divergent per-behaviour
  seam copies; share/adapt the seam maths the enemy wrap epic develops rather
  than reinventing.
- The human-like governor (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) is preserved: reaction
  cadence, W/A/D + optional reverse, seeded aim-skill noise and human-feel
  thrust presses are unchanged; wrap-awareness is a model property, not a
  scripted manœuvre.
- Use the seam when it is net-positive (Q2) — nearest-wrapped-path selection
  already yields that; no deliberate "wrap tricks".
- Do not change game physics (player/enemy/bullet wrap models); the bot's model
  must match the game, not alter it.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state (evidence)

- **Player wraps at all four edges** — `src/utils/movementModel.ts`
  (`if (x < 0) x += width; if (x >= width) x -= width;` and same for y). The
  headless eval arena drives the bot through the same `asteroidModel.tick(width,
  height)`, so the bot's own ship already wraps there.
- **Bullets wrap (game)** — `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` four-edge wrap;
  raider patrol wraps (`src/scenes/core/raiderPatrol.ts`). **Eval culls bullets
  off-field instead** (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` `offField`), and hostile fire
  there aims at the raw player position.
- **Bot treats edges as walls** — legacy `botDecision.ts` `evaluateVector`
  ("a direction is unsafe when it reaches a wall within `wallMargin`") and
  competent `steering.ts` `evaluateDirection` (same); both tuned by a
  `wallMargin` knob (`botDecision.ts:189`, `competent/tunables.ts:239`,
  `style/fitting.ts`, `tuningFields.ts:94`).
- **All geometry is raw Euclidean** — `competent/goals.ts` `nearestTarget`
  (`Math.hypot`), `competent/steering.ts` `bearingTo` / `interceptPoint` /
  `closestApproach`, `worldModel.ts` `nearestEnemyDistance` /
  `predictIncomingFire`, `botDecision.ts` distance / closestApproach.
- **Existing wrap compensation, not awareness** — `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`
  deliberately clamps spurious position jumps caused by wrap/respawn.
- **Tests assert the bot never wraps** — `botSteering.integration.test.ts`
  ("it never wraps the screen").
- **Enemy wrap epic in flight** — AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 makes enemies wrap and fire
  across seams (blocked child slices AH-0MVKXBV0O005Q77P, AH-0MVKXBWDY008R0YH,
  AH-0MVKXBSAD003VRMF, AH-0MVKXBTNJ003F1TC, AH-0MVKXBXQX003S7K5,
  AH-0MVKXBZ5N007LKH4); once it lands, a wrap-blind bot fails to aim or dodge
  seam fire at all.

## Desired change

Give the bot's decision layer a single, shared wrap-aware (torus) model:

1. **Wrap-aware steering primitives** in the decision layer — a wrapped bearing /
   delta helper alongside the existing raw geometry, with a small hysteresis at
   nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths so targeting does not flip duplicates every
   tick; use it for the four steering/clearance tests (legacy + competent) and
   for `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint`.
2. **Wrapped nearest-selection** — `nearestTarget`, `nearestEnemyDistance` and
   the collect/engage/evade distances use wrapped distance; evade flees across a
   seam when that is the safest separation.
3. **Seam-aware prediction** — `predictIncomingFire` and the closest-approach
   solves run on the torus; verify `hazardVelocity` still clamps only true
   teleports.
4. **`wallMargin` retirement** — remove/re-purpose the knob and its style-fit
   mapping; keep saved configs loading.
5. **Eval parity** — wrap enemy bullets, aim hostile fire along the shortest
   wrapped path, and update `arena.test.ts` so metrics capture wrap-aware play.
6. **Docs & tests** — update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` / `docs/EVALUATION.md`; add
   the wrap-scenario tests from AC1–AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — wrap-aware `evaluateDirection`
  (no wall-margin wall test), `bearingTo`, `interceptPoint`, `closestApproach`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `nearestTarget` and goal distances on
  the wrapped torus.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `nearestEnemyDistance`, `predictIncomingFire`
  on the torus.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — collect/engage/evade distances
  and the evade flee direction.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — legacy `evaluateVector`, legacy aim/aim-delta and
  closest-approach paths.
- `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts` — re-verify the wrap-jump clamp under the
  torus model; adjust only if double-compensating.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts`,
  `src/ai/style/fitting.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`,
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — retire/re-purpose `wallMargin`; keep config
  loading tolerant.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` + `arena.test.ts` — wrapped enemy bullets, seam-aware
  hostile aim, parity tests.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` — describe the wrap-aware model.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/worldModel.test.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`, plus a
  dedicated wrap-geometry unit test module.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** — "Enemies should be aware of the wrap around" (open
  epic with blocked child slices). Enemy counterpart: wrap-aware enemy movement
  and seam-aware enemy fire. Directly relevant — share the seam maths/helpers
  and sequence work so the bot and enemies land coherently.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed) — the wrap model the game's bullets use.
- **AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO** — "Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour
  tree, predictive dodge/aim" (completed) — the competent layer this change
  extends.
- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** — "Demo bot: human-like input limits" (completed) —
  the human-like governor whose look-and-feel must be preserved.
- **AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN** — "Predict enemy movement (bot)" (completed) — the
  hazard-velocity tracker whose wrap clamp interacts with the torus model.
- **AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV** — "Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay
  objects as the main game" (open) — bot/gym parity concern; watch for overlap.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: duplicate flapping** — when the raw path and the wrapped path are
  nearly equal, a naive min-distance choice can flip between two seam
  duplicates every tick; mitigated with a small hysteresis/tolerance at near-equal
  lengths (the commitment layer already adds some hysteresis).
- **Risk: `wallMargin` migration ripple** — the knob appears across tunables,
  style-fitting, the tuning UI and saved `bot-tuning.json`; handle removal so
  saved configs keep loading, update the fit mapping, and document the behaviour
  change for old configs.
- **Risk: double-compensation** — `hazardVelocity` clamps wrap jumps today;
  once positions are modelled on the torus, verify the tracker only clamps true
  teleports/respawns and never swallows legitimate seam re-entry.
- **Risk: eval divergence** — the headless arena must mirror the game's wrap
  physics or wrap-aware behaviour earns no eval credit; keep the parity change
  minimal (bullet wrap + seam aim) and covered by `arena.test.ts`.
- **Scope-creep guard** — out of scope: game physics changes, non-torus
  pathfinding/routing, scripted wrap manœuvres, and any enemy/wrap changes
  beyond the arena-parity bump. Anything extra found becomes a linked work item,
  not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: dimensions** — the bot already receives playfield dimensions via
  tunables (`playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight`, 960×540), so the torus needs no
  snapshot changes.
- **Assumption: seam maths reuse** — the enemy wrap epic (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8)
  will have developed wrapped-delta helpers; reuse/adapt rather than duplicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of wrap-awareness for the bot? (a) Movement/steering only. (b) +
  seam-aware aim/targeting. (c) Full torus model — plus seam-aware threat/hazard
  prediction." — Answer (Map): "(c) Full torus model". Source: producer reply on
  the work item (comment thread AH-C0MVR682R00022NOC). Research: steering walls
  in `botDecision.ts` + `steering.ts`, raw Euclidean geometry throughout
  (`goals.ts`, `worldModel.ts`, `behaviours.ts`), enemy wrap epic
  AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 in flight.
- Q2: "Should the bot deliberately *use* the seam as a manœuvre, or merely stop
  avoiding edges?" — Answer (Map): "Use it when net-positive". Source: producer
  reply on the work item. Research: nearest-wrapped-path selection yields
  net-positive seam use naturally; no scripted trick, human-like governor
  unchanged.
- Q3: "Should the headless eval arena be brought to wrap-parity with the game so
  eval measures wrap-aware play?" — Answer (Map): "Yes". Source: producer reply
  on the work item. Research: `arena.ts` culls enemy bullets off-field and aims
  hostile fire at the raw player position — both diverge from the game.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** – Enemies should be aware of the wrap around (open)
- **AH-0MU8FOQ7L005AII0** – Core Asteroid Entity + Unit Tests (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
