# Test-first: pure Arc chain eligibility (red tests)

Parent: Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69) — covers
parent AC1, AC2, AC4 (pure-helper half) and AC7.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want pure unit tests that pin how the Arc chain filters its
candidate list, so the rule "auto-targeting offence picks enemies, never the
inert `asteroid` world hazard" is proven without booting a Phaser scene, and a
future AOE weapon cannot silently regress into firing on rock.

## Context

`src/utils/aoe.ts` owns the pure AOE geometry. `findNearestTarget`
(`src/utils/aoe.ts:139`) and `selectChainTargets` (`:172`) currently skip only
`alive === false`; there is no target-kind filter of any sort. The Arc chain in
`CombatScene.onAoeFired` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:721`) is built from
`this.getEnemyEntities()`, which includes asteroids, so the bolt spends itself
on rock.

This item is written **first** (TDD): its new expectations are expected to FAIL
(red) until the sibling implementation item, *Shared auto-target eligibility rule and Arc wiring*, lands. It also adds the tests for the **new shared pure
module** (`src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`) that the implementation item creates.

## Scope

1. **New shared rule tests** — `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts`:
   - `INERT_WORLD_HAZARD_ARCHETYPES` contains exactly `['asteroid']` and does
     **not** contain `lane-traffic` (which stays targetable, matching the
     Orbital Strike precedent AH-0MVU3341U001B40T).
   - `isEligibleAutoTarget(entity)` is true for a live `'scout'`, true for
     `'lane-traffic'`, true for an entity with **no** `archetype` (gym
     `TrainingTarget` / historical stubs), false for `'asteroid'`, false when
     `alive === false` (including an asteroid that is already dead).
2. **Predicate-filtered geometry tests** — extend `src/utils/aoe.test.ts`
   (`describe('findNearestTarget')`, `describe('selectChainTargets')`):
   - `findNearestTarget` with an `accepts` predicate skips a **nearer excluded**
     candidate and returns the farther eligible one.
   - No predicate supplied → legacy live-only behaviour is unchanged (existing
     tests must stay green).
   - `selectChainTargets` with an `accepts` predicate: a field
     `origin → enemy A → asteroid → enemy B` within the reach budget returns
     `[A, B]` — the excluded rock **neither absorbs nor breaks a hop**.
   - An excluded rock inside the hop budget does **not** consume a link: with
     `maxLinks = 3` and only two eligible enemies, the chain length is 2.
   - The hop **reach** limit still applies to eligible targets only; an eligible
     enemy beyond `maxHopDistance` from the previous hop is not chained.
   - No eligible candidate → `[]` (and `null` from `findNearestTarget`).
   - Determinism: equal distances resolve to the earlier candidate, exactly as
     today (the existing tie-break is not reordered by the filter).

## Out of scope

- Production code changes (implementation item owns those).
- Scene-level behaviour (sibling scene-regression test item).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts` exists and asserts the shared
  exclusion list contains only `asteroid`, that `lane-traffic` stays eligible,
  that an absent `archetype` stays eligible, and that dead entities are never
  eligible.
- **AC2** — `src/utils/aoe.test.ts` asserts a nearer excluded candidate is
  skipped by both `findNearestTarget` and `selectChainTargets`, and that a chain
  in the order `enemy → asteroid → enemy` within reach returns both enemies.
- **AC3** — `src/utils/aoe.test.ts` asserts an excluded rock inside reach does
  not consume a chain link and does not break the chain, and that the hop reach
  budget still applies to the eligible hop.
- **AC4** — Legacy behaviour is pinned: calling `findNearestTarget` /
  `selectChainTargets` **without** a predicate returns exactly what it returns
  today (live-only filtering), so other callers cannot regress.
- **AC5** — Before the implementation item lands, the new expectations fail
  (red) for the missing rule/predicate; after it lands, `src/utils/aoe.test.ts`
  and `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts` pass. Evidence recorded in the
  completion comment (red → green).
- **AC6** — Full-text-free unit gate: the changed scope (`/skill:test` changed
  scope) passes.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts` (new)
- `src/utils/aoe.test.ts`
- Reference only: `src/utils/aoe.ts`, `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`
  (the existing `isOrbitalStrikeTarget` rule the new module must generalise).

## Dependencies

None (test-first item; blocks the implementation item).

# Test-first: Arc-vs-asteroid scene regression tests

Parent: Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69) — covers
parent AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 (gym half), AC5, AC6 and AC7.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want a scene-level test that proves the Arc never damages,
shatters or farms an asteroid, while the Nova, Mortar and Smart Bomb pulse are
provably unchanged — so the fix cannot silently widen or narrow the exclusion.

## Context

`CombatScene.onAoeFired` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:709`) builds the Arc
chain from `selectChainTargets(x, y, this.getEnemyEntities(), aoe.chains + 1, aoe.radius)`

# Shared auto-target eligibility rule and Arc wiring

Parent: Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69) — covers
parent AC1, AC2, AC4, and the behaviour behind AC3.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the Arc bolt to strike the nearest **enemy**, hop across
rocks to further enemies, and do nothing at all when the field holds only rock
— so my timed weapon is spent on threats and cannot farm minerals or Extra
Lives off asteroids I never aimed at.

As a designer, I want that rule defined **once** in a pure shared module and
consumed by the shared combat core, so the game and every gym cannot drift
(gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1) — exactly as the Orbital Strike fix
(AH-0MVU3341U001B40T) did for the single-target strike.

## Context

- Arc is the only auto-targeting AOE weapon: `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.arc.aoe`
  (`trigger: 'onFire'`, `radius: 60`, `chains: 2`) is dispatched through
  `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `CombatScene.onAoeFired`
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:709`), which calls
  `selectChainTargets(x, y, this.getEnemyEntities(), aoe.chains + 1, aoe.radius)`
  and then applies damage, the along-path bullet clear, the bolt VFX and the
  impact feedback **from that one selection**.
- `src/utils/aoe.ts` filters only `alive === false`.
- `Asteroid.archetype === 'asteroid'` (`src/entities/Asteroid.ts:274`);
  `PlayScene.getEnemyEntities()` returns asteroids too.
- Precedent: `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts` already excludes the
  `asteroid` archetype (`ORBITAL_STRIKE_EXCLUDED_ARCHETYPES`) and explicitly
  notes "every other weapon may still hit asteroids".
- A destroyed **small** asteroid pays one mineral plus a roll at the
  configurable Extra Life chance, which is why the every-beat auto-chain is
  also a power farm.

## Implementation sketch (minimal end-to-end slice)

1. **New pure shared module `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`** (layering: `src/utils`
   may not import from `src/scenes`, verified):
   - `INERT_WORLD_HAZARD_ARCHETYPES = ['asteroid'] as const` — the rock hazard
     only; `lane-traffic` stays targetable.
   - `isInertWorldHazard(archetype?: string): boolean` — an **absent**
     archetype is never a hazard (gym `TrainingTarget`s and historical stubs
     stay targetable).
   - `isEligibleAutoTarget(entity)` — `alive !== false` **and** not an inert
     world hazard. Identify by archetype **string**, never `instanceof`.
2. **`src/utils/aoe.ts`** — add an optional trailing `accepts?: (target: T) => boolean`
   parameter to `findNearestTarget` and `selectChainTargets` (default:
   live-only, so existing callers and tests are byte-for-byte unaffected);
   thread it through the hop loop. Keep both helpers pure and deterministic
   (existing earlier-candidate tie-break preserved).
3. **`src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`** — delegate
   `isOrbitalStrikeTarget` / `ORBITAL_STRIKE_EXCLUDED_ARCHETYPES` to the new
   shared module, keeping both exports and their exact behaviour so the
   existing Orbital Strike tests and callers stay green. Update the module JSDoc
   to say the rule is now shared with Arc.
4. **`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`** — in `onAoeFired`, pass
   `isEligibleAutoTarget` to `selectChainTargets` so the chain, the path
   (`path`), the along-path bullet clear, `applyArcChainEffect`,
   `spawnArcChainVfx` and `resolveChainImpactFx` all describe the same
   filtered strikes. Update the JSDoc on `onAoeFired` /
   `applyArcChainEffect` and `selectChainTargets` to state the rule.
5. **No tuning, no per-scene copies**: fire rate (1 beat), radius (60 px),
   chain count (2) and the catalogue description are unchanged; the change
   lives only in shared code, so `PlayScene` and every gym (including
   `GymWeapons`, whose `TrainingTarget`s have no archetype) inherit it.

## Out of scope (linked, not folded in)

- Extending the exclusion to Nova / Mortar / the Smart Bomb pulse (parent
  Assumption A1 and Appendix Q1 — recommended: no).
- Adding a "bolt fizzles" cue when no eligible enemy exists (a silent beat is
  the existing empty-field behaviour).
- Re-tuning Arc's power budget; that belongs to Weapon upgrades are too
  powerful (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` exists, is pure (no Phaser, no
  scene import), exports the inert-hazard list plus `isInertWorldHazard` and
  `isEligibleAutoTarget`, and excludes only `asteroid`; an absent archetype is
  eligible.
- **AC2** — With an asteroid nearer the ship than a ship enemy, firing Arc
  strikes the enemy and leaves the asteroid `alive`; on an
  `enemy → asteroid → enemy` line inside 60 px both enemies take damage and the
  rock takes none (parent AC1, pinned by the sibling scene test item).
- **AC3** — A chain hop whose geometrically nearest next candidate is a rock
  continues to the next eligible enemy within the unchanged 60 px reach and the
  unchanged link budget (`chains: 2` → primary + 2 hops) (parent AC2).
- **AC4** — A field holding only asteroids is a full no-op: no damage, no chain
  VFX, no impact cue, no asteroid kill accounting — identical to the existing
  empty-field behaviour (parent AC3).
- **AC5** — The bolt path/VFX and the along-path bullet clear are derived from
  the filtered chain, so no segment is ever drawn to a rock.
- **AC6** — The rule exists in exactly one place: `CombatScene` consumes the
  shared helper, no gym or scene defines its own copy, and
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (the duplicate-body guard)
  still passes (parent AC4).
- **AC7** — `selectChainTargets` / `findNearestTarget` remain backward
  compatible: with no predicate supplied they behave exactly as before, so
  existing callers and their tests are unchanged and green.
- **AC8** — `strikeTargeting` behaviour is unchanged (its existing tests stay
  green) and the Orbital Strike rule now delegates to the shared module rather
  than duplicating the archetype list.
- **AC9** — Nova, Mortar and the Smart Bomb pulse still damage asteroids inside
  their areas; the cannon still destroys an asteroid on contact (parent AC5,
  pinned by the sibling test item).
- **AC10** — Enemy-ship scoring/drop/wave accounting is untouched, and asteroid
  rewards via other means are unchanged (parent AC6).
- **AC11** — The changed-scope gate (`/skill:test` changed scope) passes; the
  full suite passes at the dev-push gate (parent AC7, AC9).

## Key Files

- `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` (new)
- `src/utils/aoe.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- Reference only: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/entities/Asteroid.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by both test-first items:
- Pure Arc chain eligibility (red tests)
- Arc-vs-asteroid scene regression tests

# Document the auto-target eligibility rule

Parent: Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69) — covers
parent AC8.

## Goal (user story)

As a designer, I want the auto-targeting rule written down in the design docs
and in the code JSDoc, so a future AOE weapon cannot silently regress into
"fires on asteroids" and the docs never promise behaviour the code does not
deliver.

## Context

The docs currently describe Arc as "strikes the nearest enemy"
(`docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 table row A3, line 962) and
`src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts` records that "every other weapon may still
hit asteroids". After the Arc fix, that sentence is the standing rule for all
**auto-targeting** offence, so the docs need one explicit statement of scope:
auto-targeting picks enemies; aimed/area weapons may still hit rock.

## Scope

1. **`docs/Game Design Document.md`**
   - §4.4 AOE weapons table, row **A3 (Arc)**: add that asteroids are never
     targets — the chain hops across/around a rock so the link budget and the
     60 px reach are unchanged — and name the shared helper.
   - The **"AOE weapons — Nova, Mortar and Arc"** appendix paragraph
     (line ~992): add the standing rule — *auto-targeting offence targets live
     enemies only and skips the inert `asteroid` world hazard; aimed fire,
     Nova, Mortar and the Smart Bomb pulse may still hit asteroids* — plus the
     shared-module reference and the coverage line (add the new test file).
2. **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`**
   - The asteroid/world-hazard section (near the Orbital Strike / AOE notes,
     ~line 166 and the `CombatScene.onAoeFired` divergence note ~line 1710):
     state that the `asteroid` archetype is excluded from **all** auto-targeting
     offence (Arc chain + Orbital Strike), and that excluding by archetype
     string keeps it identical in the game and the gyms.
3. **`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`**
   - The `GymWeapons` row (and its divergence table entry "AOE practice
     targets"): note that the `TrainingTarget`s carry **no** `archetype`, so
     they stay valid Arc targets and the gym still visibly demonstrates the
     bolt under the new rule.
4. **Code JSDoc** — the helper module, `selectChainTargets`/`findNearestTarget`
   and `strikeTargeting.ts` each state the rule and cross-reference the parent
   item (the JSDoc text itself lands with the implementation item; this item
   verifies it is present and accurate, and fixes drift).
5. **`README.md`** — review only: it lists Arc in the drop/weapon inventories
   but makes no claim about targeting. Record in the completion comment that no
   README change was needed (or make the minimal correction if a targeting
   claim exists).

## Out of scope

- Player-facing text: the catalogue description already says "strikes the
  nearest enemy" (parent Assumption A4), so `src/utils/weapons.ts` copy needs
  no change.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — GDD §4.4 row A3 states that Arc never targets asteroids, that hops
  skip rock without consuming a link, and references the shared helper.
- **AC2** — The GDD AOE appendix paragraph states the standing auto-targeting
  rule, distinguishes auto-targeting from aimed/area weapons, and lists the new
  coverage test file.
- **AC3** — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` states that the
  `asteroid` archetype is excluded from auto-targeting offence (Arc + Orbital
  Strike) and why exclusion is by archetype string (gym parity).
- **AC4** — `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records that `GymWeapons`' archetype-less
  `TrainingTarget`s remain Arc-targetable, so the documented divergence still
  holds.
- **AC5** — JSDoc on the shared helper, on `selectChainTargets` /
  `findNearestTarget` and on `strikeTargeting.ts` states the rule and
  cross-references AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69; no doc claims a behaviour the code does
  not have.
- **AC6** — `README.md` is reviewed with the outcome recorded in the completion
  comment (no stale targeting claim remains).
- **AC7** — Documentation assertions that are machine-checked
  (`src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`, any docs assertion suites) still
  pass under the changed-scope gate.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`
- `./README.md`
- Reference only: `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`,
  `src/utils/aoe.ts`, `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`

Blocked by *Shared auto-target eligibility rule and Arc wiring* (documents the
implemented behaviour, not the intent).

## Goal (user story)

*As the balancing agent, I want the pre-change 100-game campaign batch recorded
before any weapon data is edited, so the post-change comparison in
AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T is meaningful rather than a guess.*

Parent: **Weapon upgrades are too powerful** (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T) — this is the
measurement half of producer answer Q3 = B, and it is **ordering-critical**: it
must land before the catalogue/curve data edits (children "Trim level-0 output
of non-cannon weapons" and "Flatten WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS curve").

## Context

- Harness: `scripts/evaluate.mjs` batch mode (`npm run evaluate -- --batch`),
  documented in `docs/BALANCING.md` §Quick start. Default is 100 deterministic
  games with the `competent` policy on the **full campaign** (not skirmish).
- Current intended-experience artefact: `src/data/experience-targets.json`
  (`targetsVersion` 1, datasetVersion 2, campaign, 100 games, seeds 1–100).
- `eval-output/` is git-ignored, so the numbers must be **recorded in the work
  item** (and later in `docs/BALANCING.md`) — the artefacts are kept locally as
  the comparison reference only.

## What to do

1. Confirm the tree is at a clean commit and there are **no** uncommitted weapon
   data edits.
2. Run the batch: `npm run evaluate -- --batch --games 100` (default
   `--out eval-output`). Do **not** use skirmish or a different game count — the
   comparison must be same-sweep.
3. Copy the artefacts to a dated, clearly-named directory
   (`eval-output/baseline-<YYYY-MM-DD>/balance-report.json`, `.txt`) so a later

   and `avoidableHits`.

   `experience-targets.json` centres (it should, modulo drift already tracked by
   the harness); if it does not, record the delta and raise it — it decides
   whether the later re-baseline is a correction or a consequence of this change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A 100-game campaign batch is captured with the default competent policy at
  a recorded commit hash, and the artefact pair is retained locally under a
  dated `eval-output/baseline-*/` path.

# Goal

As a maintainer, I want `npm run capture` to work through the new Hangar War screens, so I can still capture gameplay footage that includes the Hangar scene, Hex map scene and defence report — not just the classic arcade run.

## Context

**Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)** introduced two new game scenes:
- `HangarScene` — the player-facing hangar screen where players browse unlocks and deploy
- `HexMapScene` — the ring map with known-ahead hex intel

These scenes are registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts` and reachable from the Menu via the new 'Hangar War' button (`src/scenes/MenuScene.ts`, the `🛠  Hangar War` control at lines ~306–339, focus-registered at line 571), but the capture tooling has no knowledge of them. `npm run capture` currently only knows how to:
1. Press Enter on the focused 'Play Game' menu button → `PlayScene`
2. Use registered gym scenes from `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` (including `GymHangar` and `GymHexWar`)
3. Use dev scenarios (boss, boss-four-hits, defeat)

The bot does not know how to reach HangarScene or HexMapScene from the menu, so any capture that tries to enter Hangar War will fail or record a blank/frozen screen.

## Scope

1. **Menu navigation path** — extend the capture bot (scripts/capture-bot.mjs / capture-gameplay.mjs) to recognise and press the 'Hangar War' menu button when a Hangar War capture path is requested. The Hangar War button is at the same level as 'Play Game' and requires a Tab or similar key to shift focus (MenuScene uses FocusManager).

   Verified focus order (`FocusManager` registration order in `MenuScene`: lines 263 / 565 / 571 / 574 / …): `Continue` (only when a checkpoint exists) → `▶  Play Game` → `🛠  Hangar War` → `👁  Watch Demo` → …. `Play Game` is the default focus, so **one Tab then Enter** reaches the hangar; a fresh capture browser profile has no checkpoint, so `Continue` is absent. A profile that *does* carry a checkpoint needs two Tabs — either handle that explicitly or document the assumption.

2. **Scene registration** — register `HangarScene` and `HexMapScene` in the capture system so they can be targetable scene keys (analogous to how gym scenes are registered in `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` in scripts/capture-scenes.mjs). These are parameterised scenes (they need hangar-war payload data), so they should follow the same pattern as `GymLevel` / `GymFodderEnemies` in `PARAMETERISED_GYM_SCENE_KEYS`.

   Verified constraint: the in-page director (`src/core/captureDirector.ts`, `resolveSceneEntry`) validates a requested key through `resolveWatchableSceneEntry` **and** additionally requires it to be among the gym scenes discovered on the page. The Hangar War screens are boot-registered shipped scenes, not gyms, so a registry change alone is not enough — the director needs a shipped-scene path that skips the gym page-discovery check. All three scenes accept `{ payload?, storage?, demo?, demoDwellMs? }` launch data and every field has a shipped default (`createDefaultPayload`), so no setup payload is *required*.

3. **Scene config entries** — add `HangarScene` and `HexMapScene` entries to `examples/scenes.json` so multi-scene captures can include them. The entries need valid `setup` payloads (hangar-war payload for HangarScene, ring/hex data for HexMapScene).

   Verified: a minimal `{"demo": false}` setup captures the static, player-facing screen; a hangar-war `payload` is optional because the shipped default payload is used when none is supplied. A `{"demo": true, "demoDwellMs": …}` entry additionally captures the shipped attract traversal (map → deploy → defence report → hangar) end to end.

4. **Defence report scene** — **RESOLVED (verified in code): it is a separate scene, not a sub-mode.** `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` owns `DEFENCE_REPORT_SCENE_KEY = 'DefenceReportScene'`, and `PlayScene` starts it after a hex deployment (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` ~line 5053). Two consequences: (a) it needs a capturable scene key; (b) it is currently **missing from the `scene` list in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`**, so that `scene.start('DefenceReportScene', …)` transition (and any in-page capture switch to it) silently does nothing at runtime. Registering it at boot is part of this work.

## Implementation Sketch (verified against the current tree)

1. `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — add a frozen `HANGAR_WAR_SCENE_KEYS`
   (`DefenceReportScene`, `HangarScene`, `HexMapScene`) and a
   `CAPTURABLE_SCENE_KEYS` = watchable gyms + those; teach
   `resolveWatchableSceneEntry`/`sceneSetupFieldsFor` about the shipped keys
   and add `demo` (boolean) / `demoDwellMs` (positive integer) setup fields,
   rejecting gym-only setup fields on a shipped target with
   `setup-not-supported`.
2. `src/core/captureDirector.ts` — accept shipped scene keys without the gym
   page-discovery requirement (they are boot-registered), and expose a
   read-only `activeSceneKeys()` so the CLI can verify the expected screen is
   live. Keep everything inside the `isCaptureDirectorEnabled()` dev gate so
   `npm run check-bundle` stays green.
3. `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register `DefenceReportScene` in the boot scene
   list so both the shipped between-sortie transition and the in-page capture
   switch work.
4. `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — add a `--hangar` capture mode whose start
   plan is `Tab` → `Enter` (reusing `START_KEY_GAP_MS`), a fixed-length window
   (`--duration`, default 15 s) because a static screen has no run-end signal,
   and a post-gesture assertion that `HangarScene` is active — a lost Tab must
   fail with an actionable `CaptureSetupError`, never record the menu as a
   successful clip. Leave the default demo path byte-for-byte unchanged.
5. `examples/scenes.json` — add `HangarScene`, `HexMapScene` and
   `DefenceReportScene` entries with minimal valid setups.
6. `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — document `--hangar`, the new targets, their
   setup fields and the `Continue`-checkpoint two-Tab caveat; update any README
   list of capture paths.
7. Tests — registry/resolver/setup validation (`scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`),
   shipped-key director behaviour (`src/core/captureDirector.test.ts`), CLI
   arg/start-plan coverage (`scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`), a gameConfig
   registration test, and docs guards pinning the new entries.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — the scripted input plan
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — the capture CLI (menu navigation, Enter gesture)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — scene registry, parameterised keys, watchable keys, setup schema
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` — registry / setup-schema guard tests
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` — dev-gated in-page `start(key)` director (needs the shipped-scene path)
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — registered scene classes (`DefenceReportScene` is missing)
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — where the Hangar War button lives (lines ~306–339, focus at 571)
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — new hangar screen
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — new hex map screen
- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` — the between-sortie defence report screen
- `examples/scenes.json` — multi-scene capture config
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — hangar screen model/renderer helpers
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — hex-map model/renderer helpers
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — capture documentation to extend

## Dependencies

- None — this is a capture-tooling fix.
- Related to the Hangar War epic: **AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE** (children AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1, AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2, AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP)

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run capture` completes successfully when the capture config targets HangarWar scenes; no blank/frozen output.
- `HangarScene` and `HexMapScene` are registered as known scene keys in `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` and can be used as targets in `examples/scenes.json`.
- Valid `examples/scenes.json` entries exist for HangarScene and HexMapScene with realistic setup payloads.
- The bot navigates the Hangar War menu entry (Tab + Enter) and enters the hangar screen.
- `DefenceReportScene` is registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`, so the between-sortie transition and the in-page capture switch can actually start it.
- `npm run build` and all tests pass.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (or equivalent) is updated to document the Hangar War capture path.
## Producer review response (2026-11-03, manual audit rejection)

**Rejection:** "When running npm capture the bot never leaves the hangar war
loadout selection screen."

**Verified root cause (reproduced end to end).** Build Candidate D inserted the
**🛠 Hangar War** control between `▶ Play Game` and `👁 Watch Demo` in the
`MenuScene` focus order, so the default capture's single **Tab** now lands on
**Hangar War** instead of **Watch Demo**. `Tab → Enter` therefore opened
`HangarScene`, whose non-demo screen is static, silent and emits no run-end
signal, so `npm run capture` recorded the loadout selector until
`--max-duration`. Reproduction: `node scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs
--max-duration 30000` (dev worktree) recorded a static clip → probe
"sampled frames are static (no motion)", "audio track is silent", and the
`.capture.json` join anchor reported `runStartedAtEpochMs: 0` (no run ever
started). This was the demo-path regression the previous change missed.

**Fix delivered (additive; the `--hangar` deliverable is preserved).**

1. The default demo start plan is now **Tab → Tab → Enter**
   (`captureStartKeys('demo')`), reaching `Watch Demo` again, and the capture
   **asserts `PlayScene` is active** before recording (`evaluateDemoActivation`)
   so a lost gesture or a future focus-order change fails loudly instead of
   recording a static screen.
2. The `--hangar` clip now **leaves the loadout selector**: after showing the
   hangar screen for a short hold it hands the bot to the **shipped Hangar War
   attract traversal** (its hex-map hub started with `{ demo: true }` — exactly
   what `MenuScene.startHangarWarDemo()` does), so the clip continues through
   the hex map and the weakest-adjacent-hex deployment. The traversal start is
   asserted too (`activeSceneKeys()` reports `HexMapScene`), so a clip resting
   on the static hangar screen can never be accepted. No traversal rule is
   duplicated in the capture tooling.

**Added acceptance criterion:**

- `npm run capture` (the default demo path) starts `PlayScene` and fails
  loudly if it does not; `--hangar` leaves the hangar screen and the shipped
  traversal (hex map → deployment) runs and is proved.

# Intake brief — Flaky unseeded PlayScene.test.ts integration assertions (boss phase advance, level-advance alive count)

**Headline:** Make the `PlayScene` integration boots reproducible (explicit run seed plus no live animation frame while a test asserts), so the boss-phase-advance and level-advance alive-count assertions only go red on a real regression.

## Problem statement

Two exact-count assertions in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load — one run each on two consecutive full-suite runs at dev tip `18f51aca9` — even though both passed in the immediately preceding gates on the same tree. A red full-suite gate therefore no longer means a real regression: it blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full-suite gate** — a flaky red gate blocks every `dev` push and burns a retry cycle plus a triage item.
- **Maintainers of `PlayScene`, wave spawning and the boss encounter** — they need these two assertions to keep proving the real contract (phase advances exactly once per hit pool; a fresh wave starts fully spawned).

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want `PlayScene.test.ts` to be reproducible, so an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by a random red run.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the boss-phase and wave-alive assertions to stay exact (not weakened to "at least one"), so a genuine double-advance or a lost spawn is still caught.*

## Existing state (evidence)

- Failure 1 (run A): `PlayScene — boss encounter (AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ) > AC2 — the 4-phase health bar depletes and advances the phase on hits` — `AssertionError: expected 3 to be 2` at `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:2028` (`boss.getPhaseNumber()` after `damageBossPhase(scene, boss)`).
- Failure 2 (run B): `PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AC5 — clearing a level advances to the next level automatically` — `AssertionError: expected 8 to be 9` at `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:1107` (`scene.getAliveCount()` vs `wm.waveEnemyCount()`).
- Both passed in the child-finish gates for AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD and AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV on the same tree, so they are intermittent rather than deterministic.
- `bootPlay()` (`PlayScene.test.ts:654`) and `bootPlayAtBoss()` (`:669`) inject no run seed **and** leave the harness's resumed live `requestAnimationFrame` loop running. `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` (`:684`) does both: it calls `result.scene.setRng(FIXED_RNG)` and `result.booted.game.loop.stop()`.
- `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:5908`) draws `randomSeed()` (backed by `Math.random()`) when nothing is injected, and `setRunSeed()` (`:5798`) is only read at the next `create()`. `bootSceneWithLevels()` (`:547`) calls `scene.scene.restart()` then `await advanceGame(...)`, so a seed must be injected *before* that restart (the pattern already used by `bootWithHordeWave()` at `:6261`).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` boots deterministically with fixed deltas but **resumes** the live loop afterwards, so real frames with wall-clock deltas can still run at any `await` boundary.
- `getAliveCount()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:5241`) counts spawned-and-alive entities, so a wave whose later groups are released on the wave timer (rather than by `finishSpawnAnimations()`) can legitimately be one short at the instant the test asserts.
- Precedent in this same file: AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R (asteroid heading) and AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU (Robotron horde kill) both required a **reproduced seed** before a fix was accepted; a green re-run was explicitly rejected as evidence.

## Candidate mechanisms (to confirm during implementation)

1. **Unseeded run seed** — drop rolls, power-up rolls, enemy behaviour and spawn planning differ per run, so an exact phase index / alive count can land one out.
2. **Resumed live rAF loop** — a real frame with a large wall-clock delta can advance wave timers, spawn release and collisions between the harness's `await` points on a loaded host. Seeding alone cannot fix this.
3. **Spawn-window timing** — `finishSpawnAnimations()` completes the wormhole transit of *already released* entities; a group still pending on the wave timer is not counted yet, which matches the observed 8-vs-9 shortfall.

## Desired change

Give every `PlayScene` boot helper in the integration file a deterministic, reproducible starting state (explicit run seed injected before `create()`/`restart`, and no live animation frame while the test drives and asserts), after reproducing each named failure on pre-fix code with a recorded seed. Keep the two assertions exact where determinism makes them exact; where a test must tolerate in-flight state, assert the invariant instead, with a comment saying why.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reproduction recorded before the fix:** a specific run seed is found that makes *each* of the two named assertions fail on pre-fix code, and is recorded in a work-item comment (command + seed + observed failure). A green re-run on its own is not accepted as evidence.
2. **Deterministic boots:** every `boot*` helper in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` that boots a `PlayScene` injects an explicit deterministic run seed before `create()`/`restart` (through one shared helper, mirroring `bootPlayWithAsteroid()`'s `FIXED_RNG` and `bootWithHordeWave()`'s `setRunSeed`), so repeated runs of any suite in the file observe identical initial state.
3. **No live frame during assertions (producer-confirmed as part of the required deterministic boot, not an optional extra):** `bootPlay()` and `bootPlayAtBoss()` — and any other helper whose suite asserts exact counts — stop the resumed live rAF loop for the duration of the test, mirroring `bootPlayWithAsteroid()`, so no wall-clock frame can advance state between `await` points.
4. **Both named assertions pass deterministically:** three consecutive `/skill:test --scope changed` runs that include `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, with no seed injected by the environment, plus the `dev`-push full-suite gate. (Producer-confirmed verification channel; ad-hoc `vitest` and single-file runs remain out of scope.)
5. **Invariants where in-flight state is legitimate:** any test that must tolerate in-flight bullets or spawn-animation lag asserts the invariant instead of an exact instantaneous count (e.g. phase index monotonicity, or alive count after the wave's spawn window is fully released), with a comment explaining why.
6. **Test-only change:** no behaviour change in `src/` production code; only existing seams are used (`setRunSeed`, `setRng`, `game.loop.stop()`).
7. **Documentation updated:** the in-file comments explain the deterministic boot and the seed policy; any related docs are updated to reflect the changes.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** agent-initiated runs go through `/skill:test` only; no ad-hoc `vitest`, and single-file runs are not a sanctioned reproduction channel (per AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R).
- **Blast radius:** the file has ~35 `boot*` helpers across 34 `describe` blocks and ~300 tests. Seeding changes the initial state of every suite in the file, so each affected suite must be re-verified; if a suite depended on unseeded variety, adjust that suite (with a comment) rather than leaving it flaky.
- **Do not weaken the assertions** to "at least one" just to go green — they must still catch a real double phase advance or a lost spawn.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is out of scope (managed by the ship pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — boot helpers (`bootPlay` `:654`, `bootPlayAtBoss` `:669`, `bootPlayWithAsteroid` `:684`), `bootSceneWithLevels` `:547`, `bootWithHordeWave` `:6261`, and the two assertions (`:1107`, `:2028`). Needs a shared seeded-boot helper plus loop-stop wiring.
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — deterministic boot that resumes the live loop; needs reading (not changing) to confirm loop-stop semantics.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `setRunSeed` `:5798`, `setRng` `:5781`, `_initRunSeed` `:5908`, `getAliveCount` `:5241`; read-only, existing seams.
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()`; read-only.
- `src/test/powerUpTestFixtures.ts` — `createSeededRng` re-export used by the existing `FIXED_RNG` fixture.

## Related work

- AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R — same file, asteroid heading flake; fixed by seeding `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` and stopping the loop (completed).
- AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU — Robotron horde kill flake; fixed by seeding + isolating the kill (completed).
- AH-0MVF6VZG9000AN6E — per-describe boot reuse in heavy suites (completed).
- AH-0MVF6XQIC005RY3P — deterministic boot harness (fixed-delta boot, loop stop/resume).
- AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — where the two failures were discovered.
- AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3, AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ — the parent ACs of the two failing assertions.
- AH-0MV5L6BVN005DP4I — hold-full mineral pause that can freeze `tick()`; AH-0MURBER4L00821RR — `finishSpawnAnimations` seam.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** neither failure is a genuine gameplay regression (both passed on adjacent gates; the same code paths have dedicated deterministic suites). If the reproduced seed shows a real defect, raise it as a separate blocking item.
- **Risk (latent order-dependence):** seeding every suite may expose existing dependence on random layouts; treat each exposure as a found bug, not as a reason to leave the helper unseeded.
- **Risk (diff size):** seeding 35 helpers could balloon the diff; keep it to one shared helper plus one-line call-site changes.
- **Risk (scope creep):** production RNG behaviour must not change; any temptation to add a new production seam is out of scope.
- **Risk (verification cost):** the file has a 120 s per-test ceiling and 300 tests; use `/skill:test --scope changed` for the three-run loop and let the `dev`-push gate cover the full suite.
- **Scope-creep guard:** a general "no unseeded boot helper anywhere in the repo" guard test is a useful follow-up, not part of this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Answers recorded 2026-11-01 from the producer via interactive reply (all three recommendations accepted).

- **Q1 — Scope of seeding:** AC1 says *every* `boot*` helper (~35 across 34 `describe` blocks) must inject a seed. Options: (a) seed all helpers file-wide via one shared helper and re-verify each suite; (b) seed only the helpers used by the two flaky suites first, then extend file-wide in the same item; (c) seed only the two flaky suites and file the rest as a follow-up item.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the unseeded helpers are the latent flake source the item exists to remove, and a single shared helper keeps the diff small.
  **Answer (producer):** (a) as recommended. Source: interactive reply. Research: enumerated the helpers and `describe` blocks in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`; the existing seeded patterns are `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` (`setRng` + `game.loop.stop()`) and `bootWithHordeWave()` (`setRunSeed` before `scene.restart()`).
- **Q2 — Live rAF loop:** the item's "Likely cause" names only the unseeded RNG, but `bootPlay()`/`bootPlayAtBoss()` also leave the harness's resumed live loop running, which seeding cannot fix and which matches the "only under full-suite parallel load" signature. May AC1 be widened to cover stopping the live loop as well (as `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` already does)?
  **Recommended:** yes — deterministic boot must mean both a fixed seed and no wall-clock frame while the test asserts.
  **Answer (producer):** yes. Source: interactive reply. Research: `src/test/gameHarness.ts` stops the loop for its fixed-delta boot and then resumes it; `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` already stops it per test.
- **Q3 — Verification channel:** AC2 asks for "3 consecutive full-suite runs of the file", but repo policy forbids ad-hoc `vitest` and treats single-file runs as an unsanctioned reproduction channel. Should the evidence be three consecutive `/skill:test --scope changed` runs that include the file, plus the `dev`-push full-suite gate?
  **Recommended:** yes — that is the sanctioned channel and it also covers the full-suite requirement.
  **Answer (producer):** yes. Source: interactive reply. Research: `AGENTS.md` test-execution policy; AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R explicitly rejects single-file runs as a reproduction channel.
**Research note (no question asked):** AC1's reproduction-before-fix requirement is not an invented constraint — it is the precedent set in this file by AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R and AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU, both of which rejected a green re-run as evidence. Source: those work items' descriptions.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0** – Test-skill runner no-ops: no .pi/test-config.json suiteCommands for vitest (completed)
- **AH-0MUXZ4CNS009RV40** – Full-run capture wait, tail and cap (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvib7pd50029zy1, ac1, ac2, ac5, add (+362 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0murber4l00821rr, ac1, ac2, ac5, acceptance (+342 more)

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan skill, 2026-11-01)

**Pre-check:** `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` → `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium — Medium risk is above the auto-skip risk set). Effort/risk values are unchanged from the intake estimate (Small / Medium / 10-25).
**Approval gate:** `plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate` → `request_approval: false` (approval is requested only for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk), so the plan was produced and reviewed without an approval pause.

This item owns (a) its two named assertions (boss phase advance `:2028`, level-advance alive count `:1107`) and (b) the file-wide seeded/loop-stopped boot contract.
- **Overlap:** the *shared deterministic boot helper* itself. Its AC9 already says "if AH-0MVX2DKC8001RRM4 has already landed a file-wide seeded-boot helper, reuse it instead of introducing a second one".

# Railgun is too powerful (AH-0MVY0A23A009MRK3)

> Operator seed intent: "Railgun at level 0 should not pass through enemies. At
> high levels it can start to pass through."
>
> Producer decisions (recorded 2026-11-03, see Appendix): **Q1 = A** (lower the
> base damage budget `5 → 1`), **Q2 = A** (pass-through starts at level 1),
> **Q3 = A** (this item owns the Railgun's level-0 value; the trim child's row
> is updated to it).

## Problem statement

The Railgun's identity — a slow, long-range line-piercing tracer — is priced as
a **damage budget of 5 hit points at level 0**, so on the first shot of a run it
already destroys five 1-HP ships in a line. At a 3 s cadence the budget is the
only strength lever the weapon has, and 5 makes it a crowd-clearer the moment it
drops instead of a heavy single shot that grows into a piercer.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the Railgun to feel like a heavy, deliberate shot whose
  pierce is something the weapon *earns* as it levels, not something it arrives
  with.
  - *As a player, I want a level-0 Railgun shot to hit the first enemy it meets
    and stop, so a fresh pickup is a precise, heavy single shot rather than a
    free line sweep.*
  - *As a player, I want the first Railgun upgrade to let the tracer punch
    through the ship it destroys into the next one, so levelling the weapon is
    what turns it into a line weapon.*
- **Designer / balancing agent** — wants the Railgun's level-0 output to sit
  inside the 40 % weapon-trim bound and the shipped `maxHitPoints` seam to be the
  only mechanism involved, so balance stays testable and cannot fork between the
  game and the gyms.
- **Developer (game + gyms)** — wants no new pierce mechanism: the change must
  ride the existing shared seam, so `PlayScene` and every gym keep running the
  same code.

## Existing state

The pierce is entirely the `maxHitPoints` **damage budget**
(`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `railgun` entry: `maxHitPoints: 5`). The shared seam
(`CombatScene.onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:410-430`)
spends one hit point per enemy, remembers the enemy in
`PlayerBullet.damagedEnemies`, and only lets the bullet continue when it
**destroyed** the enemy *and* budget remains. Level resolution
(`resolveWeaponDefinition`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts:1210`) adds the shared
`maxHitPoints` upgrade curve (base 0, cap 5, k 0.25, discrete, **no weapon-level
clamp**) on top of the base budget.

Resolved Railgun budget by level (today vs. after this change):

| level | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| today | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 8 | 9 | 9 | 10 |
| after | **1** | 2 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 6 |

Two tests currently pin the old intent: `src/utils/weapons.test.ts:1183`
("the catalogue's deepest pass-through") and `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts:823`
("a deeper base damage budget than the wave laser"). `docs/Game Design
Document.md:1220` also states the base budget is **5**.

## Desired change

1. `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.railgun.maxHitPoints`: `5 → 1`. That alone means a level-0
   shot spends its single hit point on the first enemy it meets and is consumed
   (kills one 1-HP ship; chips 1 HP off a tougher one) — **no pass-through**.
2. Leave the shared `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS.maxHitPoints` curve untouched, so the
   first upgrade resolves the budget to **2** and pass-through begins at
   **level 1** (one extra 1-HP kill), then grows 3 / 4 / 4 / 5 … as above.
3. Rewrite the two pinning tests to the new intent (level-0 budget 1 and no
   pass-through; level-1 budget 2 starts piercing; monotonic growth), and add a
   shared-seam test proving a level-0 shot destroys only the first of two 1-HP
   enemies in a line while a level-1 shot destroys both.
4. Update the prose that states the old value (`src/utils/weapons.ts` railgun
   comment + player-facing description, `docs/Game Design Document.md:1220`).
5. Bullet flight, visuals, cadence and feel metadata are unchanged: `E(2,16)`
   cadence (3 s), keep the "slowest, heaviest" comparison to the Wave Laser by
   **cadence**, not by budget depth (the Wave Laser's own redesign
   AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ stops using the damage budget altogether).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.railgun.maxHitPoints` is `1` and
  `resolveWeaponDefinition('railgun', 0).maxHitPoints` is `1`; the catalogue and
  level-curve tests assert both (no test claims the Railgun has the deepest base
  budget).
- [x] A level-0 Railgun shot does **not** pass through: in the shared seam, a
  shot that destroys a 1-HP enemy is consumed and a second 1-HP enemy directly
  behind it takes no damage (test in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`,
  running the shipped `CombatScene` path).
- [x] Pass-through starts at level 1: `resolveWeaponDefinition('railgun', 1)
  .maxHitPoints` is `2` and a level-1 shot that destroys a 1-HP enemy continues
  into the enemy behind it; the resolved budget is monotonically non-decreasing
  in level and saturates at 1 + the shared curve's asymptote.
- [x] The level-0 value is inside the trim bound of **Trim level-0 output of
  non-cannon weapons (AH-0MVWAVKS0005P9VN)** (≤ 60 % of the recorded baseline
  `5`, i.e. ≤ 3) and that item's `railgun` row is updated to the new value with
  its realised percentage.
- [x] Only the Railgun's budget changed: every other weapon's level-0 values
  (including the cannon's frozen values), the shared upgrade curves, fire
  cadences, lifetimes, bullet visuals, muzzle flash and impact FX are
  byte-identical to the pre-change snapshot.
- [x] Gym↔game parity holds with no scene or gym edit (the seam is shared); if
  any unavoidable edit is needed, it is recorded with its reason in a work-item
  comment.
- [x] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (the net-new weapons paragraph
  and any other statement of the old `5` budget), and the player-facing weapon
  description — with no residual claim that a level-0 Railgun pierces.
- [x] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (the dev-push gate
  is the enforcer; no CI/CD pipeline tests in scope).

## Verification

1. Build: `npm run build` (TypeScript, no emit) — must stay clean.
2. Changed-scope tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` →
   `run_tests.py`, changed scope) covering at least
   `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — direct `vitest`/`npm test`
   invocations are not permitted for agent runs.
3. Full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate (infrastructure, not an agent
   run) before any push to `dev`.
4. Optional visual confirmation: the `GymWeapons` practice targets show a
   level-0 tracer stopping at the first target and a levelled tracer continuing
   through it.

## Constraints

- **Single source of truth:** edit only catalogue data (and its comments/tests)
  — no scene-local constants, no new pierce/budget mechanism, no changes to
  `src/scenes/core/`.
- **Do not retune the shared curve.** `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS.maxHitPoints` is
  shared with the Wave Laser until AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ lands; the ramp must
  follow from the base-1 change alone.
- **Do not touch acquisition pacing**, other weapons, AOE radii, or the
  spawn-invulnerability pass-through (a separate shipped behaviour).
- **Ordering:** this edit must land **after** the pre-change balance baseline
  **Capture pre-change weapon balance baseline (AH-0MVWAVJJG003S0XF)**, or that
  epic's before/after comparison is contaminated (dependency edge added).
- **Repository boundaries:** do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other
  agent-infrastructure directories.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `railgun` catalogue entry: `maxHitPoints: 5 → 1`;
  rewrite the "greater than the wave laser's" budget comment, the top-of-file
  weapon doc block if it states the depth, and the player-facing `description`
  so it does not claim a level-0 pierce.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — "Railgun is a single slow shot with the
  catalogue's deepest pass-through" (~line 1183) rewritten to the new intent
  (single aimed shot, level-0 budget 1, slower than the Wave Laser by cadence).
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` — "the Railgun carries a deeper base damage
  budget than the wave laser" (~line 823) rewritten: level-0 budget `1`,
  level-1 budget `2`, monotonic growth to the curve asymptote.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — shared-seam coverage: level-0 shot
  stops at the first 1-HP enemy; level-1 (budget 2) shot destroys both.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — confirm no railgun-specific budget
  expectation breaks (currently none beyond the Wave Laser's).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 net-new weapons paragraph (~line 1220)
  and any other statement of the Railgun's base budget.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` / `src/powerups/icons.ts` — only if a hint or comment
  claims the Railgun pierces at level 0.

## Related work

- **Trim level-0 output of non-cannon weapons (AH-0MVWAVKS0005P9VN)** — its
  planned `railgun` row (`5 → 3`, "HP budget is the only lever at a 3 s
  cadence") is **superseded** by this item's value `1`; the row and its realised
  percentage are updated there (producer answer Q3 = A). A dependency edge now
  records the ordering.
- **Weapon upgrades are too powerful (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T)** — the 40 % trim
  epic this item feeds (its AC1/AC2 lever for the Railgun).
- **Capture pre-change weapon balance baseline (AH-0MVWAVJJG003S0XF)** —
  ordering-critical: this edit must land after the baseline run.
- **Wave Laser redesign (AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ)** — plans to drop the Wave Laser's
  damage budget (single red beam, 1 damage, stops at first intercept), which
  would leave the Railgun as the only `maxHitPoints` consumer; the rewritten
  tests must state the Railgun's intent directly rather than only comparing it
  with the Wave Laser.
- **Wave Laser should have limited hit power (AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S)** — the
  completed item that introduced the `maxHitPoints` budget semantics this change
  reuses.
- **5 net-new weapon types (AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW)** — shipped the Railgun with
  the budget of 5.
- **Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA)** / **Railgun launch muzzle-flash VFX
  (AH-0MVQ6C1YL003HU9K)** — the Railgun feel package; unaffected (visual/audio
  metadata only).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (net-new weapons, wave-laser budget
  paragraph), `docs/BALANCING.md` (Euclidean ladder rows only — no budget table
  entry for the Railgun).

## Related work (automated report)

> Produced by the `find-related` skill from keyword search; the manually
> curated list above is the authoritative one. The generic matches below
> (`power-ups`, `pass`) are low-signal and kept only for traceability.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X** – Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene (completed)
- **AH-0MT7USMWN0071UF5** – Clarify enemy pass-through and bullet-blocking rules in GDD (Wall vs Dive Bomb) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: enemies, level, levels, pass, powerful (+3 more)
- `README.md` — matched: enemies, level, levels, pass, powerful (+3 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: enemies, level, levels, pass, railgun (+2 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Level-0 throughput drop is large** (5 → 1 damage on a 3 s cadence): the
  Railgun becomes the weakest level-0 weapon by output until upgraded. This is
  the producer's explicit choice (Q1 = A); the trim epic's measured batch gate
  (**Post-change measured gate and targets re-baseline
  (AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL)**) is the feedback loop if it reads as too weak.
- **Pierce arrives on the first upgrade** (Q2 = A). If playtesting finds level 1
  too early, the lever is a Railgun-specific budget override — a follow-up item,
  explicitly **not** in scope here.
- **Assumption:** no gym or scene file needs an edit (shared seam consumed by
  both); any unavoidable edit is recorded with its reason.
- **Assumption:** the operator's "high levels" intent is satisfied by growth
  from level 1 onward, with the budget saturating near `6` — the old level-0
  ceiling of `5` is no longer reachable at level 0.
- **Scope-creep guard:** redesigning the seam ("one enemy only"), retuning other
  weapons or the shared curve, and re-balancing the trim epic are out of scope —
  record them as linked work items instead of widening this one.
- **Test-churn risk:** several tests pin the old comparison ("deeper than the
  wave laser"); each rewrite must preserve the *intent* (a heavy, slow,
  line-piercing weapon) rather than deleting the assertion.
- **Related-report noise:** the automated `find-related` sweep surfaced generic
  matches (`power-ups`, `pass`); the authoritative related list is the manual
  one above.
- **Failure mode:** with a budget of 1 the shot still chips exactly 1 HP off a
  2+ HP enemy and is consumed, so a level-0 Railgun is a single-target poke; if
  the level table is edited without re-running the level-curve tests, the
  "deeper than the wave laser" assertions fail loudly rather than silently
  drifting (they are rewritten, not removed).
- **Assumption:** line numbers cited in this brief are approximate and will
  drift; anchor edits on the quoted assertion text, not the numbers.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should a level-0 Railgun shot do?" — Answer (producer, interactive
  reply 2026-11-03): **A** — lower the base damage budget `5 → 1`: the tracer
  spends one hit point on the first enemy it meets and is consumed; it never
  reaches anything behind it. Source: interactive reply.
  Research: the budget-only path is `CombatScene.onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:410`), so no new mechanism is needed.
- Q: "From which level should the Railgun start passing through?" — Answer
  (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-03): **A** — level 1, i.e. the first
  upgrade adds a hit point (budget 2) and the shared curve stays unchanged.
  Source: interactive reply. Research: `curveValue` (`src/utils/curve.ts`) is
  discrete and rounded, so base 1 + the shared variable resolves to `1, 2, 3,
  4, 4, 5 …`.
- Q: "How should this relate to the trim child's Railgun row?" — Answer
  (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-03): **A** — this item is authoritative
  for the Railgun budget; the trim child's `railgun` row
  (**AH-0MVWAVKS0005P9VN**) is updated to the value chosen here. Source:
  interactive reply. Research: that item's plan table proposed `5 → 3`, which
  still passes through three 1-HP ships and therefore did not satisfy this
  item's goal.
- Duplicate check (2026-11-03): `wl search railgun` found **AH-0MVWAVKS0005P9VN**
  (partial overlap — its planned budget of 3 still pierces), **AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S**
  (completed, introduced the seam) and the feel-package items (unrelated). No
  item satisfies this item's acceptance criteria, so it is not closed as a
  duplicate.

## Implementation record (2026-11-03)

All eight acceptance criteria are met; see the completion comment for the
evidence trail (commit hash, tests, docs). Summary of the delivered change:

- `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.railgun.maxHitPoints` `5 → 1`; the shared

- **Trim child row updated:** **Trim level-0 output of non-cannon weapons

## User story
As a player I want each collected and upgraded weapon to fire on its own deterministic Euclidean rhythm, so that the superposition of all active weapons forms an emergent, evolving groove, and I want bullet visuals and fire sound to stay exactly in sync.

## Design decisions (agreed with producer)
1. The Euclidean pattern is the cadence itself, not a decoration. patternFor(weaponId, level) is a pure, deterministic function returning { k, n, rotation, stepMs }. Same weapon + same level => same rhythm => same sound (consistency).
2. VFX/SFX sync by construction: the fire event is the onset; bullets, muzzle flash and fire cue dispatch on the same frame. No decoupled audio schedule.
3. Irregularity is the feature: gaps within a pattern are uneven (e.g. E(5,8) has 1- and 2-step gaps). Weapons are not required to fire on a regular beat.
4. Upgrades morph the pattern: the fire-rate upgrade walks a (k, n, rotation) ladder so the rhythm can change shape (density and/or phase), not merely speed up. Morphs land on the next bar downbeat (bar-boundary morph rule).
5. Grid: patterns live on the shared 16th-note lattice at 80 BPM (187.5 ms steps); one bar = 4 beats = 16 steps. Bar-aligned n in v1 (n such as 8 or 16, i.e. divisors of the bar); accidental polymeter (n = 3 or 5 lanes) deferred. The lattice is the scheduling solvent, not a metronome: onset sets are irregular within it.
6. Consistency: one fire cue per weapon (already true); the only thing that varies is when, deterministically per (weapon, level). No per-tick voice-flavour roulette.
7. Explosions unchanged: keep the shipped snap-to-next-16th explosion accent (setExplosionBeatClock) and its per-tick cap. Weapon-kill impacts are off-grid by construction (fire time + flight time), so the musical offset is deliberate; fire-time events (onFire/onRandom AOE such as nova, arc, mortar) already detonate on-lattice with zero delay. Do NOT remove or retime the explosion accent.
8. Determinism and replay: patterns are pure functions of (weapon, level) plus game time, with no RNG and no wall-clock reads, so seeded replay is unaffected.
9. Gym parity: all changes live in shared code (beat/euclid module, Player.tryFire, CombatCoreScene._autoFire); a new Rhythm gym auditions patterns; a GYM_PARITY.md row is added.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each weapon fires only on onset ticks of its deterministic pattern; every shot time is provably an exact lattice tick.
- Same input schedule produces byte-identical shot sequences (determinism pinned by test).
- Fire VFX and fire SFX dispatch on the same frame as the fire event.
- Fire-rate upgrades keep onsets-per-minute monotonic non-decreasing in level and may change (k, n, rotation).
- Pattern changes take effect only on a bar downbeat.
- Explosion snap-to-16th behaviour is preserved unchanged (regression-guarded).
- A Rhythm gym demonstrates slow + medium + fast superposition and has a parity row.

## References
src/utils/beat.ts (grid math), src/utils/weapons.ts (subdivisions, WeaponId), src/utils/weaponLevels.ts (quantiseSubdivision, fireRate curve), src/entities/Player.ts (tryFire), src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts (_autoFire), src/audio/effects.ts (explosion accent), docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md (tempo zones and fire grid), docs/GYM_PARITY.md.

Children: pure Euclidean pattern module; fire-scheduler refactor; upgrade (k, n, rotation) ladder; Rhythm gym + parity row.
## Plan (decomposition)

Four child features, each a vertical slice (code + tests + docs) whose acceptance
criteria are stated as executable checks. Dependency order (`wl dep` edges):

1. **Pure Euclidean pattern module** (AH-0MVYA1VHT004L2O0) — no prerequisites.
   Lands the generator, the grid helpers and the canonical fixtures
   (E(3,8), E(5,8), E(2,5), maximal evenness, complement symmetry, rotation)
   that every later child asserts against. This is the test-first foundation.
2. **Weapon upgrade ladder** (AH-0MVYA291J000CK64) — no prerequisites; pure
   pattern data, so it can run in parallel with item 1.
3. **Fire scheduler** (AH-0MVYA1V8Z009SHMR) — depends on 1 and 2. Switches
   `Player.tryFire` to onset scheduling, adds the bar-boundary morph rule and
   the explosion-accent regression guard.
4. **Rhythm gym + GYM_PARITY row** (AH-0MVYA28AC006XMKL) — depends on 2 and 3.
   Auditions the six-weapon superposition through the shared scheduler.

Between phases: re-read the next child's description and acceptance criteria
before starting it. Ladder values tuned in item 2 can refine item 3's fixtures,
and the gym in item 4 asserts the shipped ladder, so re-check its documented
canonical example after item 3 lands.

Test-first ordering: there is no separate verification item because every
child's acceptance criteria are executable checks and item 1 is test-first by
construction (its tests define the pattern contract that items 3 and 4 assert).
No horizontal "all tests then all code" phase exists.

Phasing decision: the epic is Medium effort / High risk, so one four-feature
decomposition is sufficient; no multi-phase staging and no approval pause was
required (approval is requested only for Extra Large effort with High/Severe
risk).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does this epic need a fresh plan interview? Answer (agent, from evidence):
  No. The epic already records nine producer-agreed design decisions
  (comment AH-C0MVYA2HJ4007H192) and the intake pass assigned AC ownership, so
  the plan-level questions (feature boundaries, ordering, test-first) were
  answered. Final: no new questions asked of the producer.
- Q: Do the existing parity probes cover player fire cadence? Answer (agent,
  from evidence): No. `src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts:524` pins the *enemy*
  post-spawn fire cadence and `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` pins

# Goal

As a player, I want the Hangar War to actually work so its default-OFF feature flag (AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP) can be turned on (or removed) and the outer loop can ship again.

## Context

The Hangar War entry surfaces were gated behind `ai_hell_feature_flags.hangarWar` (default OFF, production-inert) in AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP because the feature currently does not work. That gate was deliberately scope-limited to entry surfaces; fixing the feature is tracked here.

## Known defect found during the gate implementation

- `PlayScene` ends a hex deployment by starting `DefenceReportScene` by key (`PlayScene.ts:5189`, `scene.start(DEFENCE_REPORT_SCENE_KEY, …)` — line refreshed during planning review; it was cited as 5067), but `DefenceReportScene` is **not registered** in the scene array in `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — so the transition cannot resolve in a shipped build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Hangar War flow runs end to end in the shipped game with the feature flag ON: menu entry → hangar → hex map → deployment → defence report → hex map.
- The root cause of the reported breakage is identified and fixed (starting with the unregistered `DefenceReportScene`), with a regression test covering the transition.
- Deciding whether to keep the flag (turned on by default) or remove it is recorded on AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Planning review findings (verified in the tree)

- **Confirmed defect:** `src/core/gameConfig.ts` registers `MenuScene, PlayScene,
  HangarScene, HexMapScene, PauseScene, HelpScene, MineralChoiceScene,
  MiniBossWheelScene, SettingsScene, TelemetryConsentScene, GameOverScene,
  LeaderboardScene, GymIndex` — `DefenceReportScene` is absent, so
  `PlayScene`'s `scene.start(DEFENCE_REPORT_SCENE_KEY, …)`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:5189`) cannot resolve in a shipped build.
- **Why the existing suite did not catch it:** the traversal/integration suites
  boot an explicit scene-class list via `src/test/gameHarness.ts`
  (`bootScene(sceneClasses, parent)`), so registration in `buildGameConfig()` is
  never exercised. The regression test must assert the shipped scene array, e.g.
  that every started scene key resolves from `buildGameConfig().scene`.
- **Flag state:** `hangarWar` defaults OFF (`src/core/featureFlags.ts`) and the
  effective value is additionally gated to dev builds; `MenuScene` hides the
  Hangar War control unless the flag resolves ON. Turning the flag on therefore
  also means deciding what happens in a production build (dev-build gate).
- **Existing coverage to reuse:** `src/scenes/hangarWarTraversal.integration.test.ts`
  already drives menu → map → deployment → defence report → map → hangar in
  test time; it can be extended to boot from the real config.

## Key Files

- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — shipped scene registration (the fix site)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — hex-deployment exit into the defence report
- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` — report scene and its key
- `src/scenes/hangarWarTraversal.integration.test.ts` — end-to-end traversal
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene()` harness (boots explicit scene list)
- `src/core/featureFlags.ts` — `hangarWar` flag and dev-build gate
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — gated Hangar War entry surface

## Implementation notes (2026-11-03)

**Root cause of "it doesn't work", verified in the tree.** Two defects broke the
player loop:

1. `PlayScene` starts `DefenceReportScene` after a hex deployment ends, but the
   scene was absent from `buildGameConfig().scene`, so `scene.start(...)` was a
   silent no-op and the loop died after the first deployment. This was already
   fixed in the tree by AH-0MVWMUQUC003WXF5 (commit 7b5d2b7a); what was missing
   was the guard that would have caught it. The traversal suites could not catch
   it because they boot an explicit scene-class list via `src/test/gameHarness.ts`
   and never exercise `buildGameConfig()`.
2. **The hangar had no route to the hex map.** `HexMapScene` has carried the
   `◀ HANGAR` row since AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2, but `HangarScene` had no mirror: a
   player entering the Hangar War from the menu could only launch a blind
   deployment at the weakest hex, so the known-ahead ring intel — the reason the
   map exists — was unreachable until after a first blind sortie. AC1 lists
   `hangar → hex map` explicitly, so a `⌗ HEX MAP` navigation row was added
   (model + renderer + scene handler), making the two screens one click apart in
   both directions as GDD §8.2 describes.

**Assumption recorded (AC1 wording).** AC1's `hangar → hex map` edge is read as a
real navigation edge, not just a screen list; that is why the `⌗ HEX MAP` row was
added rather than only asserting the existing post-report path. If the producer
prefers the original blind-deploy entry, the row is a self-contained removal.

**Flag decision (AC3).** Recorded on AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP: the flag is **kept**
as a kill switch and its default flipped **ON**; the dev-build gate on the
*effective* value is removed so the shipped (production) build runs the Hangar
War, while the *writer* (dev toggle) stays dev-only.

**Verification.** New `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` boots the
real `buildGameConfig().scene` array with the flag ON and walks
menu → hangar → map → deployment → defence report → map. New assertions in
`src/core/gameConfig.test.ts` pin that every scene key a shipped screen starts
resolves from the shipped array, and that every registered scene boots under its
own class name.

# Goal

As a player deploying the fleet into a Hangar War hex, I want the run to start with **only the ship's default weapon** — no additional hangar starting weapons pre-equipped — so the run begins from the shipped minimal kit and any extra weapon is a deliberate choice I make in the hangar, not something forced on me.

Raised by the producer's manual review of the epic (audit of AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE, 2026-11-02T08:47Z): *"The player should start with no additional weapons in the loadout, just the default weapon."*

## Context

- Today a fresh hangar-war payload defaults `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` to `['spread']` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` `createDefaultPayload`, `DEFAULT_STARTING_WEAPON_ID`), `resolveActiveLoadout`/`equipLoadout` force at least one weapon (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`), `toggleHangarWeapon` refuses removing the last equipped weapon, and `applyHangarWarDeployment` permanently equips each `startingWeapons` entry on the run's player. The result: every deployment begins with the Spread Cannon already permanently equipped, which is the "additional weapon" the producer is objecting to.
- The **default weapon** is the ship's permanent cannon (always active, never a starting weapon).
- Producer decision (this item): the default loadout is **empty**. The `spread` starter stays **owned** by the fleet and remains selectable in the hangar's deployment/loadout selector; it is simply not equipped by default. Owning/buying a starting weapon never auto-equips it.
- This supersedes the GDD §8.1 sentence "the fleet starts minimal — one basic hull, one starting weapon": the fleet still **owns** the starter starting weapon, but the **deployed loadout** starts empty. Update the docs to state the new rule.

## Scope

- Default payload/active loadout: no starting weapons ('spread' remains an owned, unequipped starter).
- `resolveActiveLoadout`/`equipLoadout`: an empty starting-weapon selection is valid and round-trips as empty (do not silently substitute `spread`).
- `toggleHangarWeapon`: removing the last equipped starting weapon is allowed (loadout becomes empty) — the hangar selector must let the player unequip everything.
- `buildHangarWeaponOptions`: every owned weapon row is toggleable (no "last weapon can never be removed" disabled row).
- Deployment: `buildHangarDeployment` reports `startingWeapons: []` for an empty loadout; `applyHangarWarDeployment` equips nothing, so the run's player has only the cannon.
- Defensive parse/migration: an existing save whose loadout names weapons keeps them (no forced reset); a fresh save/default starts empty.
- Docs: GDD §8.1 (hangar economy + deployment selector), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` if it states the rule, and the module docblocks that claim "the fleet always deploys armed".
- **No other behaviour change**: hangar economy, purchases, hulls, modifiers, capture cycle and the classic campaign are untouched.

## Out of scope

- Changing the hangar catalogue entries or their prices.
- Changing the cockpit/HUD six-slot run loadout (unrelated).
- Any classic-campaign starting-weapon change.

## Tests first

Update/extend the pure economy tests (empty loadout round-trips; last weapon removable; default payload has no equipped weapon), the hangar screen option tests (all owned weapons toggleable), the deployment tests (`startingWeapons: []`; applier equips nothing → player only has the cannon) before changing implementation. Existing tests that assert "always at least one starting weapon" are updated to the new rule (never deleted to make the suite pass).

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` (default payload / `DEFAULT_STARTING_WEAPON_ID`)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` (`resolveActiveLoadout`, `equipLoadout`)
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (`buildHangarWeaponOptions`, `toggleHangarWeapon`)
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` (+ tests)
- docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.1, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fresh hangar-war payload has an **empty** `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, and a Hangar War deployment built from it carries `startingWeapons: []`.
- Deploying an empty loadout starts the run with only the default (cannon) weapon — `applyHangarWarDeployment` calls no `equipWeapon` for an empty loadout (asserted through the seam).
- The hangar loadout selector lets the player unequip every starting weapon (last-weapon row is actionable), and equipping/unequipping round-trips through `equipLoadout` without re-inserting `spread`.
- An existing persisted loadout that names owned weapons still deploys with them (no migration regression); unknown/locked ids are still dropped.
- Docs (GDD §8.1 and any module docblock claiming the fleet always deploys armed) describe the empty-default loadout rule.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate pass.

# Goal

As a player, I want clearing campaign level 2 to advance normally to level 3 instead of crashing the game, so the shipped run is playable past the second level.

Raised by the producer's manual review of the epic (audit of AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE, 2026-11-02T08:47Z): *"When I clear level 2 the game crashes, the console says: client:859 [vite] connecting..."* — the quoted line is Vite's HMR client log, not the error, so the crash must be reproduced and root-caused in this item.

## Context

- The producer was playing the shipped game in a dev build. Level 2 is `Descent` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), a ten-wave level whose **wave 10 is the mini-boss** (`miniBoss: true`); clearing it runs the shared mini-boss defeat path (`PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` → death sweep → `_finaliseMiniBossDefeat` → reward overlay + one wave/level advance), then the `'levelCleared'` transition (`_onLevelCleared` → `_startTransition(true)` → background swap + hyperspace warp).
- The epic touched shared code that this path consumes (Boss, combat effect visuals, PlayScene capture-cycle seams), so the regression may be in the level-clear/mini-boss/transition path rather than in hangar-war-only code. It may also reproduce in a hangar-war deployment that starts at level 2 (aggression 1 → `startLevel` 2).
- A deterministic headless Phaser boot harness exists (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`, used by `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts`), so the crash can be reproduced without a browser: boot `PlayScene` on the shipped campaign, clear level 2's waves/mini-boss with the harness's deterministic kill walk, and advance the transition.

## Scope

- **Reproduce first**: a deterministic test that plays/clears level 2 of the shipped campaign (mini-boss wave included) through the real `WaveManager`/`PlayScene` path and fails with the reported crash before the fix.
- Root-cause the failure and fix it in the shared code path (PlayScene / CombatScene / effects / wave or transition helpers) — never a gym-only or test-only workaround.
- Keep the classic campaign and hangar-war deployment paths both working (a hangar deployment starting at level 2 gets the same fix).
- If the root cause turns out to be in the hangar-war-only launch/level selection, fix that instead and record the evidence in a work-item comment.

## Out of scope

- Changing level-2 content, balance or wave composition.
- Unrelated refactors of the mini-boss reward/overlay.

## Tests first

Write the failing level-2 clear regression test before the fix. It must assert observable behaviour (the run advances to level 3 / the scene stays active, no thrown exception) via the public scene harness — not a source grep. If the exact browser-only failure cannot be reproduced headlessly, document the harness limitation in the work item and assert the closest observable invariant (e.g. the mini-boss reward/transition completes and the scene advances).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_damageMiniBoss`, `_finaliseMiniBossDefeat`, `_onLevelCleared`, `_startTransition`, `_beginLevelChangeWarp`)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/bossReward`/effect visuals as indicated by the stack trace
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`, `src/waves/Formations.ts` (level 2, mini-boss wave)
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` (deterministic boot), `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` (kill-walk precedent)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.hangarWar.test.ts` (hangar deployment at level 2, if relevant)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A deterministic regression test clears campaign level 2 (including its wave-10 mini-boss) and asserts the run continues to level 3 with no exception; the test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- The root cause is recorded in a work-item comment (what threw/why, and which change introduced it).
- The same code path works for a hangar-war deployment that starts at level 2 (asserted or explained if not applicable).
- The classic campaign's level 1 → 2 and 2 → 3 transitions keep their existing behaviour (background swap + warp, mini-boss reward, checkpoint save).
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate pass.
